articleTitle: A Delta Connected Hybrid STATCOM and Dc Capacitor Voltage Balance Technique Using Zero-Sequence Current
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: The parallel hybrid converter (PHC) is advantageous over the modular multilevel converter (MMC) in terms of energy storage requirement, number of switching devices, capacitors and switching losses. However, the PHC cannot be employed for static compensation (STATCOM) applications, owing to its nature of operation at a fixed modulation index (MI). The PHC utilizes harmonic injection methods (HIMs) to regulate its MI, within narrow limits. These harmonic voltages tend to be unequal, during unbalanced grid conditions (UGCs), and therefore enter the grid and distort it further. This paper proposes a new delta hybrid STATCOM (DH-SC) which inherits the advans power with the grid and hence the capacitor voltages belonging to different CLs divert from its reference value. However, the capacitor voltages get restored to its original value with the injection of unequal third harmonic voltages as mentioned above. Nonetheless, these unequal harmonic voltages enter into the grid and further degrade its power quality. This paper proposes a new delta hybrid STATCOM (DH-SC), which is capable of operating at any MI without requiring any THIMs, both during balanced and unbalanced grid conditions. The proposed DH-SC converter also inherits the advantages of PHC over MMC such as lower energy storage requirement, lesser number of capacitors and lesser switching loss.

articleTitle: A Space Vector based Pulse Density Modulation Scheme with Reduced Computational Complexity
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: Space vector based pulse density modulation (SVPDM) scheme exhibits variable switching frequency resulting in broad and continuous frequency spectrum. The spectral spreading results in harmonic performance improvement and decline of motor acoustic noise. A space vector based pulse density modulation scheme with reduced computational complexity for multilevel inverters is presented in this paper. Reduced computational complexity is achieved in such a way that the entire computation process takes place in 120° coordinate system itself without requiring the conversion to 60° or 90° systems. The scheme makes use of the concepts of sigma delta modulation and vector quantization for generating the output switching vectors for inverters. In the proposed scheme, nearest three vectors enclosing the reference vector is identified by comparing the instantaneous values of three phase reference signals. Out of the three surrounding vectors, the vector with minimum Euclidean distance is selected as the output switching vector. Simulation as well as experimental results are utilized for validating the scheme.

articleTitle: Improved Traditional Demagnetization Control of DFIG Under Balanced Grid Faults
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: DFIG based Wind Turbines are very sensitive to grid disturbances as the stator of the machine is directly connected to the grid. As per the latest grid codes, the machine has to stay connected to the grid during faults and provide reactive power support to the grid. To meet with the latest grid codes, demagnetization techniques are employed to accelerate the damping of natural flux which improves the performance of DFIG. The traditional demagnetization method is dependent on the machine parameters and fails to fully damp out the natural flux due to error in estimated parameters. The reason for the failure of the traditional demagnetization method is analyzed in this paper. Also, the effect of error in estimated parameters on flux models is studied. An improved demagnetization method is proposed and simulations are carried out to validate it. The results show the independence of the proposed method over machine parameters.

articleTitle: An Improved Pulse Width Modulation Technique for the Attenuation of Leakage Current in Five-Level Transformerless PV Cascaded Multilevel Inverter
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: This paper presents an improved pulse width modulation technique for the five-level transformerless grid connected/ stand-alone cascaded multi-level inverter (CMLI) for attenuating the magnitude of the leakage current. The improved PWM technique employs two modified reference waves for the production of five-level at the inverter output terminals. The improved PWM technique employs a single triangular wave for obtaining the five-levels at the inverter output terminals. The improved PWM technique reduced the total harmonic distortion (THD) in the grid current by shifting the harmonics to the even multiples of the carrier frequency. Due to the shifting of the harmonics to the higher order the size of the filter required at the output of the inverter terminals are reduced. The improved PWM technique attenuates the magnitude of leakage current flowing in the PV panels. The bulky elements like electromagnetic interface (EMI) and the common filter required for the five-level CMLI are reduced without the addition of any extra circuitry.

Author Keywords: Terminal Voltage and PV Multi-Level Inverter

articleTitle: Power Management Strategy Based on Vehicle Dynamics for the Performance Improvement of Electric Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: The performance of an Electric Vehicle can be improved by using a power management strategy based on vehicle dynamics. The dynamic behaviour of the vehicle is analysed using drive cycles (DC). The frequent occurrence of traffic lights in the city requires increased starting and stopping of the vehicle and hence performance of vehicle is affected along with battery life. The Ultra capacitor(UC) used with the battery can be controlled to ensure lesser stress on battery. The proposed fuzzy logic controller operates the system to allow the UC to solely supply the power requirement during frequent velocity changes and supports the battery during normal running conditions. The methodology considers the power demand and the vehicle velocity to generate the control action on the dc-dc converters. The performance of the vehicle with the controller is evaluated using simulation experiments in Matlab/Simulink. The experiment used a modified drive cycle based on a case study in Trivandrum city. The control strategy ensures energy savings and also reduces the size of the battery pack. The proposed strategy is compared with frequency sharing based algorithm and it is found to yield an energy savings of 4.38%.

articleTitle: Calculation of Unbalances in Network Shunt Capacitances of Power Distribution Systems
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: In resonant grounded power distribution systems (RGPDSs), the fault detection sensitivity relies on the unbalance current which is the result of unbalance in shunt capacitances of distribution lines. Therefore, it is required to maintain the balance in shunt capacitances where the first step is to calculate the unbalance in shunt capacitances for individual phase. This paper presents two different ways to calculate the unbalance in network shunt capacitances of different phases in power distribution networks. In the first method, the relationship between angles of phase-to-ground voltages and residual current (unbalance current) is used to calculate unbalance parts of the per phase network shunt capacitances. This method is effective for the solidly grounded, neutral earth resistor (NER) grounded and RGPDSs with a lower percentage of resonance. The second method modifies the first method considering the equivalent T-model of the power distribution line. The second method has the capability to calculate unbalances in network shunt capacitances more accurately (than the first method) for RGPDSs with a higher percentage of resonance. The developed methods are tested through simulation in MATLAB/SimpowerSystems. Simulation results indicate that the unbalance currents can be minimised to a small value using a three-phase capacitor bank where the values of the capacitor bank are selected based on the calculated unbalance using developed methods.

articleTitle: A Wide Speed Operable Multiport Solar-assisted SRM EV Drive with Integrated Driving/Charging Capabilities
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: This work presents a multiport drive capable of integrating battery, on-board PV power, SRM and utility grid for integrated driving/charging functions and offering a wider speed range operation (WSO). The system supplies propulsion power from on-board battery independently as well as with PV assistance during light to high load conditions for a variable speed profile. On-board charger (OBC) exhibits unity power factor (UPF) charging from utility grid as well as dc charging with the on-board PV power at maximum power point offering self-charging feature during stand-still conditions. Also, trikle charging on-the-go is achieved while driving with PV power under light load conditions. Closed-loop operation of the complete system is carried out and verified on a 1 hp, 100V, 8/6 SRM, 1.78 Nm SRM using simulations results.

articleTitle: Comparison Between PM Motors for an Aircraft E-pump Drive
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: Permanent Magnet Synchronous Machines (PMSMs) are widely adopted in several fields, including More Electric Aircraft applications, due to their enhanced performance. In this paper a comparison between two types of PMSMs, used to drive an oil pump for aircraft applications, is presented. A fast automatic tool for the analytical pre-design is proposed, in order to obtain a reasonable sizing of the machine. Then, finite element analysis is carried out so to accurately evaluate and compare the obtained machines. In particular, the comparison is focused on 4 key performance indexes: mean torque, torque ripple, losses and efficiency. Finally, starting from the output of the analytical pre-design, an optimization procedure based on genetic algorithms is performed.

articleTitle: Resilience of Grid-Connected Wind Farm Using a Flexible Asynchronous AC Link
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: This paper presents an integration of wind farm (WF) into the utility grid through the flexible asynchronous AC link (FASAL) to achieve better resilience and mitigate power fluctuations. An equivalent aggregated squirrel cage induction generator (SCIG) based WF of 200 MW connected to a 150 kV utility grid through FASAL is considered for performance evaluation under LLLG fault conditions using PSCAD/EMTDC based simulation. Moreover, a comparison of the performance of the FASAL system and AC link for the connection of WF is made under grid fault conditions. Under LLLG fault, the AC link experiences significantly high fluctuations and overshoots in real and reactive power, electromagnetic torque, which causes stress on the wind turbine and the gearbox. It is found that the fluctuations and overshoots are small in the real and reactive power, electrical frequency of WF, and the electromagnetic torque in the case of the FASAL system. Thus, the FASAL shows better resilience as it reaches the normal operating condition faster with fewer oscillations. Moreover, the adverse effects of the LLLG fault on the wind turbine and the gearbox are also found small.

articleTitle: Variable Band Hysteresis Controller Fed IM Drive for Switching Frequency Variation Control
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: The objective of the work is to design and implement a Variable Band Hysteresis Controller (VBHC) fed Induction Motor (IM) drive with fast dynamic response, constant switching frequency and minimal switching losses. In the new proposed VBHC strategy, the average pole voltage waveform is used to obtain the variable band in which each phase current error oscillates and hence making the switching frequency constant. The discontinuous-Bus Clamping (BC) Pulse Width Modulation (PWM) BC30 and BC60 which have minimum losses compared to existing Conventional Space Vector PWM (CSVPWM) are used for the third harmonic injected voltage and thereby in the implementation of variable band. Simulation studies to verify steady-state and transient performance of the proposed controller based VSI fed IM drive are carried out. The results obtained are verified on a 1 kW IM with the control implemented using the dSPACE-1103 kit.

articleTitle: Transformer-less Common-Ground Inverter With Reduced Components
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: This paper a proposes a five-level transformer-less inverter based on common-ground-type topology is presented. In the common-ground-type utility neutral is directly tied with negative terminal of dc source, leads to the short-circuiting of PV-to-ground parasitic capacitance. Hence it solves variable common mode voltage and leakage current issues. Additionally, this topology has the inherent voltage boosting ability based on the principle of switched/auxiliary capacitor. A simplified logic gate-based PWM strategy and control algorithm is developed to maintain the voltage across auxiliary capacitor. A laboratory prototype is developed which proves the feasibility and merits of proposed inverter topology are presented.

articleTitle: Design of PID and Model Predictive Control for Stabilization of Photovoltaic Voltage
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: Voltage stabilization of intermittent natured solar photovoltaic (PV) network is essential for making it compatible with that of load(s) accommodated after interface network(s). At the first, this manuscript presents small signal modeling of the solar PV array fed `Buck' DC to DC converter (BDDC) system by linearization around the operating point. Through this, the brief obtains open, as well as closed loop transfer functions between output voltage of the solar PV network and duty ratio (d) of the BDDC incorporating parasitic elements. The communique discusses design of the Proportional Integral Derivative (PID) controller for stabilizing voltage of the solar PV incorporating detailed manner gains tuning procedure. The writing also presents a comparison of voltage response of the solar PV as obtained with open loop, closed loop PID and the Model Prediction based control (MPC).

articleTitle: Using Magnetic Control of DC-DC SIMO Converters in LED Driver Applications
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: This work presents magnetic control (MC) applied to Single Inductor and Multiple Output SIMO DC-DC converters in parallel configuration, for use in LED lighting drivers. The proposed MC is performed using a Variable Inductor (VI) to extend the operating range of the converter in Discontinuous Conduction Mode (DCM). In order to evaluate the method experimentally, a three-channel-output SIMO converter prototype for RGB lighting control has been implemented. This work demonstrates that using MC allows the converter to extend its operation in DCM for a wider range of input voltage, compared with using a fixed inductance value, as well as using other conventional control methods such as duty cycle and frequency control of DC-DC converters.

articleTitle: Development of MPC for an Uncontrolled Prime Mover Driven SCIG based Distributed Generation System
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: A finite control based model predictive control (MPC) is developed for the squirrel cage induction generator (SCIG) fed to stand-alone load via a back to back converter. The proposed MPC can handle both source and load side variations through the combined action of both the generator and load side controllers. The generator side converter's control performance is three-stage, whose objective is to keep the dc-link voltage constant for the operating scenarios. A load voltage controller with the inclusion of an LC filter parameter is proposed to maintain the load voltage amplitude and frequency. Further, the developed scheme is flexible for various types of cost functions. The generator side converter's cost function is modeled in the rotor flux reference frame, whereas the load end converter is implemented in a synchronously rotating reference frame. The system is tested for the uncontrolled prime mover driven distributed generation scheme. The proposed scheme's efficacy is validated with a 33% variation of source and 50% load perturbation. The machine and load variables' dynamic performances are found to be satisfactory under the considered operating conditions.

articleTitle: Optimal Sizing Analysis of Battery Energy Storage System for Electric Vehicle
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: In this paper, optimal sizing of battery-only energy storage system (ESS) in EV applications is discussed. The sizing problem is formulated as minimization of battery cost subject to voltage, power and energy constraints. The problem is in general nonlinear in nature if both the series connected cells and parallel branches are unknown. Initially, keeping the number of parallel branches fixed the problem is solved as a linear programming problem (LPP) to find out the number of series-connected cells. Then it is solved as a nonlinear programming problem (NLPP) to find out both the number of series-connected cells and number of parallel branches. The results in both the cases are compared and are found to be identical. Further, along with the cost of the battery unit (BU), battery losses due to internal resistance of the cell and weight of the BU are optimized subjected to the constraints as in NLPP. Usually, LPP and NLPP methods yield non-integer solutions. To obtain integer solutions, branch and bound algorithm of integer programming is applied till integer solutions are attained. The integer solutions are optimal in comparison to those obtained by rounding up the initial solutions and not applying branch and bound method. Results indicate that with lower number of parallel branches, the cost of the battery unit decreases with an increase in battery loss.

articleTitle: State-feedback control of grid-connected RSDCHBMLI with $LCL$ filter
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: This paper presents the grid-connected operation of a single phase reduced switch single DC-source cascaded H-bridge multilevel inverter (RSDCHBMLI). The RSDCHBMLI topology with voltage boosting capacity generates 7-level waveform with minimum number of components. Unlike other multilevel inverter topologies, RSDCHBMLI doesn't require isolated DC-sources and also provides inherent isolation between the grid and inverter-side due to presence of transformers. In grid connected operation, the current injected by the RSDCHBMLI into the grid is regulated using state-feedback plus integral (SFBI) control. The SFBI control is used with a single carrier multilevel-sinusoidal pulse width modulation (ML-SPWM) method to generate switching signals with constant switching frequency. The SFBI control gives good dynamic performance with constant switching frequency operation. The harmonic distortion of grid injected current is reduced to low values. The constant switching frequency permits easier design of the LCL filter values which is used for interfacing the inverter with the grid. The selection of the filter parameter values is also presented here. The synchronization with the grid is obtained using adaptive time-delay phase locked loop (ATD-PLL) which tracks the frequency and phase changes in the PCC voltage. The inverter operation is verified for step changes in reference power to be injected into the grid, and DC voltage.

articleTitle: Optimised Reference Current Generation For Enhanced Single-phase STATCOM
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: Static compensators (STATCOMs) are conventionally used to improve grid stability by supporting reactive power. Microgrids are inherently less stable compared to conventional grids and need even better grid support infrastructure compared to conventional grids. Increase in renewable energy integration reduces the stability of the existing grid. Modern electronic loads also inject harmonics into the grid. With the emergence of power generation from solar energy with grid -connected single-phase inverter at homes, single-phase STATCOMs may be used to improve the grid stability in single-phase distribution grids and microgrids. Enhanced STATCOMs with energy storage device like a battery on its dc bus further improves the quality of grid support by providing active power for short periods along with reactive and harmonic support. Conventional methods like envelope, synchronous reference frame have been traditionally used to control the operations of a grid-connected inverter behaving as a solid-state harmonic compensator. But none of the conventional algorithms takes the physical limitations of the converter hardware into account in the control process. In this paper, an optimisation based control methodology is proposed which performs better than the existing control algorithms on many accounts. In this paper, an optimisation based reference current generation (ORCG) algorithm is proposed for the enhanced single-phase STATCOM that can generate a current reference for controlling the converter, taking various constraints and current limit into account. The proposed algorithm also inherently minimises the THD of compensated current which is an added benefit.

articleTitle: An Investigation into the Voltage Profile Pattern Variation in Distribution Networks with Increased PV Penetration
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: Increased emphasis on clean and green energy has lead to more localised/distributed generation in the network. Increase in PV penetration in the active distribution network leads to a better voltage profile across the buses, however the extent of this is analysed through several case studies in this paper. The pattern of the voltage profile is studied through simulations on MATLAB/Simulink considering PV based DGs integrated into the modified 13 bus system for cases of varying PV penetration levels, varying distances of DGs, varying distances of the substation and different load levels. Some of the cases have been briefly discussed and the observed voltage profiles have been verified using the direct load flow (DLF) method. Contrary to common understanding, it is found that for certain cases, the voltage rises with increased PV penetration and then starts declining when more PV generation is integrated into the network.

articleTitle: GA Optimized SHE and Proportional Resonant Controller Tuned Integration of Solar PV to the AC Grid using Packed U Cell Inverter
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: The design and control of an asymmetrical flying capacitor MLI are presented and discussed in the paper. A PR control technique is designed for the proper integration of the photovoltaic sources with the AC grid. Firstly, a description of the investigated topology (packed U cell five-level (PUC5)) is presented in the paper, and then the PR control technique is discussed. A 3<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">rd</sup> order LCL filter is used for the integration of solar PV to the grid purpose. MATLAB®/Simulink is used for developing the model, and the results obtained are presented and discussed in the paper. A selective harmonic technique is also used to enhance the harmonic profile. 3<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">rd</sup> and 5<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">th</sup> harmonics are eliminated using a genetic algorithm optimization technique.

articleTitle: Investigations on an SYNRM coupled to a constant power load connected to a weak grid
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: Constant power loads like electric traction load, lathe machines, grinding machines and coiler drivers are important assets to the industry. Considering that these constant power loads are coupled to motors which are connected to weak grids where voltage dips are frequent, this paper introduces a novel analysis of the effect on speed and torque of a synchronous reluctance motor connected to a constant power load on the occurrence of a voltage dip greater than the tolerable voltage dip margin for a particular operating point. The focus of this paper is to estimate the amount of reduction in speed as well as torque and changes in the other operating quantities from the set reference values if the dc bus voltage reduces below a pre specified permissible limit. Also the method of restoration of initial operating speed on the occurrence of a voltage dip is also discussed in this paper. The proposed analysis predicting the degree of changes in all the operating quantities is validated by simulations carried out in Simulink/MATLAB environment.

articleTitle: Optimal Operation of 2nd Use Battery Energy Storage System through Power Reduction Method
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: The battery energy storage system (BESS) is an epitome area of batteries, which are retired from electric vehicles (EVs). The operational cost and working life of BESS operation is dealt by 2<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">nd</sup> use power reduction operation method. The power dispatching to BESS is optimized by use of Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) algorithm to find out the global optimal solution. The state of health (SOH) caused cost increase is included to optimize the operating cost. During the dispatching of power, consistency in SOH degradation is improved. This method provides an optimal power allocation for BESS with new and retired batteries working together. Apart from this, to enhance the fault tolerant operation potential and increase the working life of retired batteries, a power reduction operation method is used. Battery systems (BSs) with different SOH could be operated efficiently, and slowdowns the fast ageing of batteries. Furthermore, BESS can continue its operation in power reduction phase, when there exists BS which could not continue its working. Thereby, this method not only improves the system stability and reliability but also provides more power throughput. The simulation results show that both power throughput and scheduling time of BESS are increased with the use of power reduction operation method.

articleTitle: Multimode Operation of a PV-Battery System fed Brushless DC Motor Drive
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: Utilization of energy storage systems along with Photovoltaic systems, can provide an efficient solution to overcome the challenges associated with renewable energy sources. This paper proposes an algorithm for the multimode operation of a Brushless DC motor drive fed using a combination of Photovoltaic System and battery-based energy storage. Based on the solar irradiation and the state of charge of the battery, the proposed algorithm identifies a control scheme wherein the entire system operates in Four different modes. The working of the PV-Battery System fed Brushless DC Motor Drive under various operating modes is presented and is verified using simulation analysis performed in MATLAB/Simulink.

articleTitle: A Hybrid Chain-Link Push-Pull Series Connected (H-CL-P2SC) M2C with DC Fault Blocking Capability
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: This paper introduces a hybrid chain-link push-pull series connected (H-CL-P2SC) modular multilevel converter for HVDC applications, especially for those considering a connection of off-shore wind farms to the grid. On the ac side, each converter phase is connected to the corresponding grid phase via a single-phase center-tapped transformer whereas on the dc side, the converter phases are connected in series. The required functionality of the chain-link (CL) inductors in other modular multilevel topologies is achieved by using the leakage inductance of each transformer. As a result, the converter does not require separate CL inductors. Since the phases are series connected on the dc side, the H-CL-P2SC requires 33.3% less cells (NCs) to withstand the same dc voltage when compared to the standard modular multilevel converter (M2C). A control strategy for the H-CL-P2SC is discussed in detail. The global and internal power balance controllers are illustrated with block diagrams. A numerical comparison between the H-CL-P2SC and other typologies is also presented. Finally, the response of the H-CL-P2SC to a dc pole-to-pole (P2P) fault is shown using PLECS simulations for a 20 MW-20 kV demonstrator.

articleTitle: A Charge Redistribution Technique for Lithium-ion Battery pack based on Active clamp Forward converter
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: A charge redistribution technique for Lithium-ion battery pack using an active clamp forward converter with asynchronous rectifier (ACFC-SR). A switch network to connect a particular cell to a converter is also presented in this paper. The ACFC-SR is operated in constant current control mode transferring the charge from the battery pack to the specific weak cell at a constant current. Generation of gating pulses and selection of the switches is presented for multi series connected battery pack. The design of filter elements is explained. A simulation study is carried out to verify the design and performance of the charge redistribution technique. The charge redistribution is verified using step by step simulation waveforms.

articleTitle: Switched Reluctance Machine Drives Based Electric Marine-Propulsion System
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: One of the major advantages of an electric propulsion system is the complete control of shaft speed without conventional mechanical arrangements such as gear-box and clutch. Also, this increases the system efficiency. Therefore, this paper presents a switched reluctance machine (SRM) based electric marine propulsion system. Initially, a small signal analysis is carried out due to the nonlinear and time varying characteristics of an SRM. Then, to control the shaft speed, this paper proposes a two-loop control scheme which consists of inner current and outer speed control loops. Here, an average current program mode scheme is used which ensures constant switching frequency unlike hysteresis controller. Also, a scheme for regenerative braking is presented to replace a lossy mechanical-braking system. Finally, numerical simulation results are presented to validate the proposed control scheme.

articleTitle: Space Vector Modulation Technique with Improved Harmonic Performance for a Five Phase Induction Motor Drive in the Over-Modulation Region
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: This paper proposes a new space vector based pulse width modulation (PWM) technique to operate a five phase induction machine fed by two level inverter in the over-modulation region with significantly low harmonic distortion and switching loss. The proposed technique is simulated in MATLAB - SIMULINK and the results are compared with the existing PWM techniques. A comparative study of the performance of the five phase drive using stator flux ripple concept with the proposed PWM technique is presented in the over-modulation region. The simulation results are experimentally validated using TMS320F28379D micro-controller platform with a custom made five phase drive system. It is found that in the over-modulation region, the proposed PWM technique results in considerably low RMS current ripple and switching power loss as compared to those corresponding to the conventional PWM techniques.

articleTitle: MODELLING AND DESIGN OF AVERAGE CURRENT FILTERED BLDC MOTOR DRIVE
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: Nowadays there is an increasing popularity for BLDC motor drives in the applications such as traction, automation etc. The digital controllers are in use for the control of BLDC motor over many years. For developing the custom designs of digitally controlled BLDC motor drive, rigorous analysis over the complete system is required. In this paper the moving average filter based current controller was developed, the design model for the BLDC motor drive which includes practical speed and current measurements are discussed. In addition, for current controller gain tuning the transfer function was derived by including the current filter dynamics. The computer simulations are carried out in MATLAB/SIMULINK software environment. To validate the analysis, the experiments were carried out in laboratory.

articleTitle: Evaluation of Battery Swapping Stations (BSS) with PV Assist for High Electric Vehicle Penetration
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: Battery recharging is an essential aspect of integration of Electric Vehicle (EVs) into the transportation framework. So far, charging stations have been considered as the primary source for recharging EVs. However, a significant time is is taken at the charging station to recharge a single EV. This problem is addressed by Battery Swapping Stations (BSS) that allow for swapping a depleted battery (DB) with a charged battery (CB). As with charging stations, the participating entities remain to be the grid, the aggregator, service station(s) and the EV owner. However, a variation exists in their interaction. In this work, a scheduling management scheme is presented for an aggregator to maximize its profit while managing BSS in a densely populated area. Furthermore, this has been explored for a varying number of requests. Furthermore, a PV assist has also been considered for BSS, where the depleted batteries may be charged through the PV assist. In both cases, with and without penalty for unscheduled EVs, in the case of no PV assist and with PV assist, results indicated that maximum profit was observed in the case of PV assist. Furthermore, more batteries were found to be available for swapping in the case with PV assist.

articleTitle: Analysis and Modeling of a Switched Inductor Based Microinverter for Single Phase Grid Connected Photovoltaic Systems
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: A novel single phase single stage microinverter topology is proposed which draws maximum power out of a photovoltaic module and feeds the power at unity power factor (UPF) to the distribution end of the Indian grid system (220 - 230 V). The inverter operates as a switched inductor based Ćuk topology for both positive and negative half cycles of the grid voltage. High voltage gain at the output stage is achieved by involving a coupled inductor having a moderate turns ratio, while ensuring the inverter to operate in discontinuous mode of conduction (DCM). Energy trapped in the leakage inductance is supplied back to the grid through the coupling capacitor used in this topology thereby improving the overall efficiency of the system. DCM strategy ensures inherent soft turn on of the power switch and the voltage stress during turn off process across the power switch is controlled by passive snubber. The operating principle of the proposed microinverter along with its detailed analytical studies have been presented in this paper. The viability of the proposed scheme is confirmed by performing detailed simulation studies under various operating conditions.

articleTitle: A Single-Stage Dual-Source Seven-Level Inverter for Grid Integrated Photovoltaic Energy Transfer System with MPPT
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: A new seven-level multilevel inverter (MLI) with dual isolated input for grid-connected photovoltaic energy transfer system (PETS) is proposed in this paper. It has six unidirectional and one bidirectional semiconductor switches for realizing the seven-level output. The MLI finds application in photovoltaic (PV) energy transfer systems, where the requirement of two isolated DC sources is fulfilled by proper solar panel management. The bidirectional switch reduces the control overburden and improves circuit compactness as compared with the cascaded H-bridge MLI. The grid-connected PETS is designed to deliver the available PV power to load, connected in the distribution bus, as well as injects the remaining active power to the grid with a unity power factor (UPF). Moreover, PETS mitigates the reactive and harmonic demand of load irrespective of PV output and maintains the grid power quality within the IEEE-519 standard. The steady-state and dynamic performance of the proposed system is validated by using MATLAB/Simulink model, and the prototype for the MLI is developed and tested in the laboratory.

articleTitle: Improved Back-Emf Detection Technique for Position Sensorless Control of Permanent Magnet Brushless DC Drive
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: In this paper, an improved back-emf zero crossing point (ZCP) detection technique for position sensorless control of permanent magnet brushless DC (PMBLDC) drive is presented. Many methods of ZCP detection have been discussed in literature for both continuous and discontinuous phase currents. In these methods, terminal voltage is sampled either during PWM OFF period or ON period for ZCP detection. The proposed method does not need to sample terminal voltage specifically during PWM OFF or ON period. It is sampled after every PWM cycle and a signal is generated which helps in ZCP detection. This technique offers advantage of simple implementation. Simulation and experimental results are presented for both continuous and discontinuous phase currents to demonstrate the efficacy of the proposed technique.

articleTitle: Analysis of Different Transition Techniques for Non-isolated Bidirectional DC-DC Converters
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: This work is aimed at making an objective comparison of the mode transition techniques reported for the non-isolated bidirectional dc-dc converters (BDCs) such as synchronous buck converter, non-inverting buck-boost converter, dual active bridge (DAB), etc. The analysis is carried out by creating a mathematical models for these transition techniques. A comparison has been made based on the type of transition technique, time requirement, and other important factors to achieve a smooth transient response during start-up and mode transition (i.e., during reversal of power flow) operations. The analysis of the transition techniques has been validated through PSIM simulations as well as experimentation for 132 V and 330 V voltages at the input and output ports for 1.5 kW of output power.

articleTitle: Multiple Sinusoidal Signal Integrators and Unintentional Islanding Controlled PV-BES System at Unbalanced Grid Conditions
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: This paper demonstrates the multiple sinusoidal signal integrators (MSSI) and unintentional islanding control for photovoltaic (PV)-battery energy storage (BES) system. The unintentional islanding event is a serious issue in the grid interactive distributed renewable energy system at failure of the distribution grid. This event causes an interruption in the supply to emergency loads. Therefore, this control and topology address the issues of power quality and provide continuous power to the emergency loads under ON/OFF scenarios of the distribution grid. The precise harmonic current tracking of nonlinear load is obtained by using the MSSI control, which is also used for the mitigation of the grid voltage pollution and gives the accurate synchronization angle at operating mode transfer under ON/OFF grid conditions. The PV-BES system comprises of a bidirectional control of BES and a DC-AC converter controlled through MSSI control in ON grid mode. However, during disappearance of the grid or OFF grid mode, a transformation-based voltage algorithm is used for islanded operation. The buck/boost controller maintains the injected current to the DC link capacitor. A hybrid seamless transfer approach is implemented utilizing rate of change of frequency over power (ROCOFOP) and the islanding/synchronization is achieved as per the IEEE 1547–2018 undated standard.

articleTitle: Fault-tolerant Electric Vehicle during Multi-current sensor failure by achieving IFOC of IM Drive
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: Electric vehicles (EVs) require greater reliability in torque accuracy for a better dynamics and safety. Any EV must meet the stringent functional safety standards of ISO 26262. However, in the case of a current sensor failure, it is more likely that the said safety standards are not met. In this article, an algorithm is developed based on the measurements of machine's terminal voltages and power constraints which ensures the required torque accuracy for a high-performance Induction Motor based EV at the event of a current sensor failure. When the sensors are healthy, standard current sensor based indirect field-oriented control (IFOC) is implemented. However, at the event of one or more number of current sensor failure, voltage sensors and power constraints based FOC is implemented. The experimental results confirm that with the proposed algorithm the drive does not lose the desired dynamics of the FOC and ensures torque accuracy at the event of a current sensor failure even during starting and high-speed operations.

Author Keywords: Fault tolerant control of Electric vehicles

articleTitle: Investigating the Effect of various Voltage Sags on Grid Supporting Inverters
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: A generational shift in the production of electricity has led to the increased penetration of power electronics based generators (DGs). Due to this, it becomes imperative that the DGs operate effectively, both in normal as well as abnormal grid conditions such as voltage sags. Most of the available literature deals with one DG connected to an unbalanced grid. An effort has been made in this paper to study the behaviour of grid-supporting inverter based DGs under varying depths of voltage sag during grid unbalances, due to phenomena such as short circuit faults. A two DG system is studied for two different cases, one having similar DG ratings but different line lengths and the other having different DG ratings with same length of line from the point of common coupling. A comparison based on simulations for different kinds of voltage sags has been presented for both DGs.

articleTitle: Bidirectional Boost Converter based Solid State Transformer for AC/DC Micro-Grid Application
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: In the existing electric power distribution network, a large number of AC/DC Micro-Grids are playing their role independently to provide the desired power supply to all the consumers. However, under short time outages, natural disasters, or sudden changes in system parameters, this AC/DC Micro-grid needs to interface with the existing power grid or with each other or to be disconnected from each other to help out for seamless power supply to all the consumers in the distribution network. Conventional, low-frequency transformer used in such network, is having so many drawbacks such as low power density, poor voltage regulation, and no control over power flow with poor power quality. Sold State Transformer (SST) is a viable solution for such applications. This paper presents a structure of SST for AC/DC Micro-Grid converter (MGC). A bidirectional boost converter and a stacked half -bridge inverter are integrated with the AC/DC Micro-Grid converter. The designed 6 KW Micro-Grid Converter has a bidirectional power flow controllability with a soft switching feature to improve the overall efficiency of the converter. The designed AC/DC MGC is simulated in PSIM/Simulink co-environment to verify it's performance indices under different operating conditions.

articleTitle: Power Factor Correction in Multi-pulse Rectifier Using Zigzag Auto-connected Transformer and Non-isolated SEPIC Converters
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: To enhance the harmonic mitigation capability of the multi-pulse rectifier, this paper proposes a multi-pulse rectifier based on harmonic mitigation technology at DC link. The conventional 12-pulse rectifier does not meet the IEEE-519 standard and hence the active power factor correction technique is employed to mitigate the harmonics. The proposed system employs two diode bridge rectifiers, each followed by a SEPIC converter, by controlling the SEPIC converter inductor current, the input line current of the rectifier can be approximated to a sinusoidal waveform. A zigzag connected autotransformer is used as a phase-shift transformer in order to provide a phase shift and inherently blocks the zero sequence components. This method reduces the total harmonic distortion and also decreases the size of the system. The proposed configuration is analyzed and simulated in the MATLAB Simulink and also implemented in laboratory. The results show that the proposed method improves the power quality by reducing the total harmonic distortion (THD) in the input line current.

articleTitle: Performance Evaluation of a State Machine based Mode Transition Strategy for Microgrids with Power Quality Issues
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: A proper control strategy is to be designed for the reduction of transients which might occur when the distributed generators (DGs) move from the grid connected mode to standalone mode and vice versa. Most mode transition control approaches proposed in literature deal with ideal grid conditions and balanced loads. The power quality is an important feature in today's power system as the loads are more sensitive and non-linear and unbalanced loads are in the rise in the system. This paper deals with the performance evaluation of a state machine based mode transition strategy under power quality issues associated such as the presence of non-linear, unbalanced, constant power loads and balanced and unbalanced voltage sags and swells. The peak transients in the output powers of a simple two inverter DG based system under seven types of the power quality issues are presented through simulations using Matlab-Simulink software.

articleTitle: Design and Control of Solar PV - Battery System Feeding AC Network with DG Set Backup
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: This work presents the design and control of PV-battery system feeding power to the AC network with diesel generator (DG) set backup at unity power factor (UPF) and the loads connected at the point of common coupling (PCC). The system improves the power factor of the AC network and the DG set to unity. Furthermore, it reduces the distortion in the currents and voltages of the AC network and DG set as par the IEEE std. 519, if any nonlinear load exists at the PCC. Moreover, it mitigates the intermittency of the PV array generation and the load demand at the PCC during the daytime operation by supplying constant power to the AC network. Hence, the variation in the PCC voltages are reduced. The PV -battery system energizes the load by operating as a standalone system if the AC grid'supply is interrupted. Furthermore, it operates as an uninterrupted power supply (UPS) if the generation of PV array reduces to zero. If the battery bank also discharges, then the DG set is connected at the PCC to energize the load. Hence, the load remains energized in all conditions. Here, the DG set operates at an optimal fuel economy zone to minimize diesel consumption and operational cost. However, it is disconnected as soon as the grid supply recovers or the battery bank charges. Therefore, diesel consumption reduces to the lowest. An extensive simulation study is performed to exhibit the performance and the seamless operation of the presented system when its working mode is sudden changes.

articleTitle: A Parameter Insensitive Rotor Angle Extraction Approach using Carrier Frequency Components by Phase Shifted Carrier PWM for PMSM Drives
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: This paper presents an anisotropy based sensorless control of PMSM using carrier frequency injection with a parameter insensitive rotor angle demodulation process ensuring higher bandwidth and robust tracking. Conventional methods make use of an additional high frequency signal which limits the system's bandwidth. In this paper, the triangular carrier wave is time shifted by one-third of its period, creating a carrier frequency rotating field. The carrier frequency current response is then used for extracting the rotor information. The effectiveness of the method is simulated in MatLab Simulink environment.

articleTitle: A New Pulsating DC-link Three-Phase Transformerless Inverter for Renewable Applications
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: In this paper, a new three phase transformerless step-up inverter with pulsating DC-link is presented for PV/EV applications. The proposed inverter provides step-up, semi single stage operation along with reduced components and size. To verify the operation of the proposed inverter a simulation model is developed and the results for closed loop operation are presented.

articleTitle: A New Architecture for Circulating Current Control in a Multi-port Hybrid Nine-Arm Modular Multilevel Converter
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: In this paper, a multi-port hybrid nine-arm modular multilevel converter is proposed for integration of an offshore wind farm into the HVDC subsea power transmission system feeding an offshore subsea oil and gas processing load. A detailed analysis of circulating current of the proposed converter is performed and accordingly, a control architecture based on a synchronous rotating reference frame is developed. The proposed control architecture regulates the circulating current at an optimal value in order to achieve a stable and efficient operation of the multi-port hybrid nine-arm modular multilevel converter. The proposed architecture incorporates control of phase angle difference between the source port and load port voltages, which is the key to regulate the circulating current magnitude. A system level simulation model has been developed on PLECS simulation software to demonstrate the performance of the proposed control architecture.

articleTitle: Performance and Temperature Estimation of Induction Motor from Transient Measurement
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: This paper presents an advanced methodology for performance and temperature estimation of an induction motor based on transient voltage and current measurement. The transient stator voltage and current of a 0.5 hp, 110 V, 50 Hz induction motor have been recorded using a power analyzer. Based on the measurements, equivalent circuit parameters and losses have been estimated employing particle swarm optimization and Genetic Algorithm. The estimated performance and temperature characteristics have been compared with the measured values. The comparison results portray an acceptable degree of accuracy of the proposed estimation technique.

articleTitle: Robust Shortest Path Planning for Aircraft using Bounded Region Voronoi Diagram
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: Flight safety and fuel consumption are major concerns of airline industry. En route civil aircraft may encounter hindrances such as bad weather patches, prohibited areas, and flight constraints. Robust path planning ensures maximum safety of the aircraft, crew members and passengers in unknown environment such as uncertain wind direction and drag from low pressure areas. This paper presents the robust path generation methodology near to the line of sight from starting aerodrome to the target aerodrome. This methodology confined the search space on the aerospace map to the nearby hindrance from the line of sight and then plan a robust path for the aircraft with the help of voronoi diagram. The voronoi diagram for the airspace map gives cells on the grid map, where each cell is equidistant from the hindrances. For these cells, the shortest robust path is evaluated using Dijkstra algorithm. The simulations for the shortest robust path on the airspace map were carried out for the proposed methodology and voronoi diagram for the full airspace map. The results obtained show that unnecessary clearances from the hindrances are avoided, and the computational time to evaluate the shortest robust path has been considerably reduced.

articleTitle: Three-Port Fourth-Order Boost Converter for Renewable Energy Application
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: This paper presents a new three-port fourth-order two-switch boost converter that integrates renewable energy sources like photovoltaic (PV) panel with battery for managing varying load power demand irrespective of variation in the weather conditions. The converter operation is explained for various modes and a steady-state with time-domain analysis is carried out to evolve the high-gain feature of the converter. A small-signal multivariable dynamic model is mathematically derived to design the control loops using the relative gain array (RGA) approach. Simulation and experimental results are given for the 24/ 48 V, 50 W system.

articleTitle: Enhancing Inverters Output Voltage Quality Via Uncertainty and Disturbance Estimator-Based Controller with a Multi-Band-Stop Filter
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: The uncertainty and disturbance estimator (UDE) algorithm has been extensively developed and applied in uncertain systems for rejecting external disturbances and addressing uncertainties. Existing works in the literature mainly focus on reducing the total harmonic distortion (THD) of inverter's output voltage feeding nonlinear loads and thus enhancing the inverter's output voltage quality. However, such existing works lack a robustness guarantee in the presence of fundamental frequency fluctuations. In this paper, a multi-band-stop filter is designed based on the UDE algorithm to reduce the total harmonic distortion (THD) of inverter's output voltage and also to provide the robustness against fundamental frequency fluctuations by modifying the values of output impedance at relevant frequencies directly. The feasibility and robust performance of the proposed control method are justified with the experiments.

articleTitle: Optimised Reference Current Generation For Single-phase Heterogeneous Active Filter
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: High electron mobility transistor (HEMT) made of materials like SiC and GaN are capable of high bandwidth operation but are currently much costlier compared to widely used silicon based IGBTs. This cost disadvantage warrants the use of a heterogeneous structure of converters to increase both operational reliability and bandwidth at a reduced cost for the same output power rating compared to a single converter. The heterogeneous active filter (HAF) consists of a low power, high bandwidth HEMT based converter paired with a high power, low bandwidth IGBT based converter. The existing selective current reference generation algorithms are optimised by completely ignoring the current limitations and bandwidth capabilities of the heterogeneous converter hardware architecture. In this paper, an optimised reference current generation (ORCG) algorithm is proposed for single-phase HAF by introducing an optimisation technique, that enables incorporating various limitations of the different types of switching devices of the heterogeneous converter.

articleTitle: A Dual-Layer-Stator Doubly Salient Permanent Magnet Machine
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: A new doubly salient permanent magnet (DSPM) machine is proposed in this paper. Different from the existing counterparts, the proposed machine employs a two-layer stator, in which the inner stator layer is used to wound armature windings and the outer stator layer is used to employ PM excitation. In this case, the armature flux will not pass through the PMs, so the reluctance of the armature magnetic path is reduced, and the armature current possesses no demagnetizing risk on the magnets. Meanwhile, the proposed machine can achieve stronger PM excitation since there is more space for PM employment. The stator can be designed with several modules and manufacturing cost can be reduced during mass production. Design optimization is conducted on a 12/8 prototype, and the electromagnetic performance is investigated. The simulation results show that this proposed machine can be designed with a high torque density, and the PMs are protected from being demagnetized.

articleTitle: Multifunctional Adaptive Control Strategy for a Standalone Hybrid Microgrid
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: A standalone hybrid microgrid is presented in this paper. This microgrid consists of an energy source of solar photovoltaic (PV) array and a diesel generator (DG) set. A battery storage (BS) is employed to balance the power within the microgrid. The DC-DC converter at the output of the PV array is controlled to extract its maximum power in all operating conditions. The microgrid is feeding power to reactive as well as harmonics producing loads. The improvement of power quality (PQ) is achieved by controlling the voltage source converter (VSC) using an improved variable zero-attracting least mean square (IVZA-LMS) adaptive based control. The output voltages of the synchronous generator (SG) based DG set are controlled by adjusting its field excitation. The simulation of the standalone microgrid is done in MATLAB/SIMULINK.

articleTitle: A Coupled Inductor Based LCD Network Integrated High Gain Quadratic Converter For Renewable Applications
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: In this paper, a continuous input high step-up coupled inductor integrated quadratic boost converter is presented for photo voltaic applications. The integration of coupled inductor to the quadratic boost converter is acquiring better attention in contrast to a boost converter in terms of continuous input current and better voltage gain. Additionally, the continuous input current reinforces the life of the photo voltaic panel and discards the placement of a capacitor which makes the system bulky. The presented converter lifts the voltage gain by N + 1 times of voltage gain of the quadratic boost converter by replacing the second inductor with coupled inductors and adding one extra capacitor and diode. The description, operating modes and steady-state analysis of the presented converter are discussed in detail. Finally, The validation of theoretical analysis is verified with simulation results.

articleTitle: Switched L-C Cell Based Interleaved Boost Converter
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: A high voltage gain interleaved boost DC-DC converter with low source current ripples is proposed in this paper. Just like in Z-source DC-DC converters, with the use of switched L-C cell in the traditional boost converter a high voltage gain is achieved in this converter. Source current ripples are minimized by adopting an interleaved gating scheme to the active switches. An exhaustive time-domain analysis is performed to establish the voltage gain features along with ripples expressions. Later the component design expression are formulated. A small-signal analysis is established to design suitable PID type controller and then to achieve closed-loop voltage regulation. A 48 V to 200 V, 75 W scale down converter verifies the high boosting capability with lesser source current ripples. Also, sample load voltage regulation demonstrating experimental results are provided.

articleTitle: Study of Forsmark-Type Voltage Transient on Power UPS in Nuclear Power Plants
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: The uninterrupted power supply (UPS) system used in Indian Nuclear Power Plants (NPP) provides 415V three-phase four-wire supply to most critical loads. These loads are required for safe reactor operation, reactor shutdown as well as during accident conditions. Hence these UPS systems have very stringent qualification requirements. The newly proposed transient test as a part of qualification given in IEEE-650 is studied in this paper. This is based on the transient incident reported at the NPP of Forsmark, Sweden. The analysis presented here brings out the possible difficulties in carrying out this transient test. It also suggests possible design modifications that need to be addressed during the design of a power UPS.

articleTitle: Analysis of DC and AC Choke Effects on Common-Mode Noise Emissions in ASD at the Frequency Range of 9–150 kHz
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: Magnetic chokes are conventionally utilized at the DC or AC side of the Adjustable Speed Drives (ASDs) to suppress low order harmonics of 0-2 kHz. Recently, the frequency range of 9-150 kHz has been noticed as a new disturbing frequency range, interfering with the distribution networks. Due to the novelty of this topic, so far, there has not been a thorough investigation for the effect of DC and AC choke configurations on 9-150 kHz emissions, especially for the three-phase ASDs. In this paper, the effect of DC and AC choke configurations on Common-Mode (CM) current emissions at the frequency range of 9-150 kHz is broadly surveyed in the three-phase ASDs. Subsequently, the comprehensive equivalent models of the system are presented for each configuration of DC and AC chokes. This investigation is based on the comparative analysis of the system's transfer functions according to the presented single-phase equivalent model, mathematical calculations, and the three-phase system circuit. Consequently, the presented approach is highly useful to minimize the drive system volume, as the designer can predict the choke configuration of the smallest size for suppressing 9-150 kHz emissions.

articleTitle: Optimal Number of Wind Turbine in Farm Layout with Power Maximization
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: Designing of wind farm layout is complex and challenging task due to its space and cost associated constraints. Usually, turbines are positioned in close proximity. Thus, the generated power of downstream turbine is affected by the wake effect produced by upstream turbine. This is challenge to power system planning and reliability forecasting. Therefore, it is a non linear constraint optimization problem. Thus, in this paper, differential evolution strategy is used to find optimal positioning and number of wind turbine for maximization of power generation incorporating wake effect. Strategy implemented have two characteristics: (a) dimension is reduced to two (b) population size parameter is eliminated. Results provide the optimal number of wind turbine in farm layout with maximization of power output.

articleTitle: Hybrid Integrator Control with Seamless Mode Transition in Solar PV-SB Based Microgrid
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: In this paper, a hybrid integrator control for solar photovoltaic (PV) array and storage battery (SB) based microgrid with seamless mode transition capability is presented. In grid-connected mode (GM), the voltage source converter (VSC) operates in the current control mode using a hybrid integrator. In the event of grid outage, the system is made to operate in a standalone mode (SM) and the VSC control shifts to the voltage control mode. In addition, the load demand is met without any interruption and the surplus solar generation is used to charge the SB using a bidirectional DC-DC converter (BDC). Furthermore, the SB supplies the load demand even under the combination of grid outage and disrupted solar power generation. By the virtue of a boost converter control, the PV array delivers peak power in both modes. MATAB based simulation results corroborate the applicability of this new control.

articleTitle: Design and Thermal Investigation of a Dual Rotor De-Coupled Stator Multi-phase Permanent Magnet Synchronous Generator for Wind power Application
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: This paper reveals the design and thermal investigation of a Dual Rotor De-Coupled Stator Multi-phase Permanent Magnet Synchronous Generator (DRDCSMP-PMSG) for wind power application. The motive of thermal investigation is to employ it for the optimal selection of various materials required for the advancement of DRDCSMP-PMSG. The Lumped Element Network Model Method (LENMM) and Finite Element Method (FEM) are used for the thermal investigation. The conclusion of the two methods exhibit good agreement. The Lumped Element Network Model (LENM) in the paper has sixteen nodes corresponding to critical parts to compute distribution of temperature in different sections of the DRDCSMP-PMSG like shaft, inner stator yoke, permanent magnet, outer stator yoke etc. Although, the accuracy of Finite element thermal model is more than the lumped element network thermal model, it takes considerable time for the improvement in machine design and simulation process.

articleTitle: Dynamic Power Coupling Analysis of Droop Based Autonomous Microgrid Using Dynamic Relative Gain Array
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: The parallel operation of various voltage source inverter (VSIs) based distributed generation (DG) units in autonomous mode is ensured by sharing the load power in a decentralized manner using (P-f) and (Q-V) droop control framework. It is well established that as the X/R ratio of the feeder impedance interfacing DGs to the point of common coupling (PCC) decreases, there exist a Strong static coupling between active and reactive powers. However, when these DGs operate in droop control scheme there may exist a dynamic coupling between their active and reactive powers. In this work, dynamic relative gain array method is used to analyse the existence of dynamic coupling between the active and reactive powers of DGs in desired frequency range by formulating a reduced order multivariable transfer function model relating active power and reactive power of each DG with respect to their voltage angles and voltage magnitude.

articleTitle: Bench-marking High Power Switching Performance of $Ga_{2}O_{3}$ SBD with SiC Devices
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: Gallium Oxide ( Ga2O3) has gained a lot of recent attention as a new power semiconductor material due to its ultra wide band-gap as compared to the conventional semiconductor material. In this context, a simulation study of switching characteristics of the Ga2O3 Schottky barrier diode (SBD) is carried out to assess its performance in power application and compared against commercially available SiC SBDs. First, the device modeling is carried out in Silvaco ATLAS followed by the circuit simulation of the modeled device in silvaco mixed mode. From the simulation results performance parameters like on-state loss, off-state loss, transient time, maximum reverse recovery current, and the switching loss is calculated and compared against the SiC diodes. The simulation results indicate the feasibility of the Ga2O3 Schottky barrier diode at larger power ratings.

articleTitle: Maximum Efficiency Point Tracking Scheme for Constant Output WPT System with Double-side LCC Compensation
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: This paper proposes a novel inductive coupled power transfer (ICPT) system, characteristic of double-side LCC compensation, switch-controlled capacitor and active rectifier. Constant current output can be realized when load changes or coupling coefficient fluctuates even in a relatively large range, which is suitable for electric vehicles (EVs) lithium battery charging. After analyzing the relationship between system efficiency and equivalent load resistance, impedance matching methods of both single-stage rectifier and two-stage interleaved rectifier are given. It is found that by reasonably adjusting the angle of MOSFETs in the rectifier, the magnetic coupling mechanism can realize approximate maximum efficiency point tracking (MEPT), thus improving the power utilization rate of EVs charging system.

articleTitle: Modified Voltage and Frequency Control of Parallel-Connected Grid-Forming Inverters by Virtual Synchronous Machine Controller
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: With higher penetration of Distributed Energy Resources (DERs) into the utility power grid, the power control architecture of the grid must be revisited. The main reason for this is that DERs mostly interface with the grid through power electronics (i.e. inverters), whereas traditional centralized grid-forming has been majorly achieved by Synchronous Generators (SG). By employing a Virtual Synchronous Machine (VISMA) controller, benefits such as communication-less and independent power control can be achieved concurrently with maintaining power grid standards (stable voltage and frequency constraints). However, the VISMA controller cannot operate under conditions where the central grid is absent, especially for the black-start condition. In this paper, a modified VISMA (called Mod-Visma) is proposed, which incorporates the missing voltage and frequency regulation outer loops into the baseline VISMA control architecture. The performance of this modified controller is validated in MATLAB/Simulink.

articleTitle: Improved Operational Schemes for MSC-GCCI Architecture used in Large Solar PV Plants
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: This paper proposes the operational strategies, control schemes, modeling, and architecture of Master-Slave Configured Grid-Connected Centralized Inverters (MSC-GCCI) for large Photovoltaic (PV) power plants. The issues of dynamic power-sharing among the master-slave inverters with fault-tolerant operations are addressed, and improved control scheme and operational strategies for MSC-GCCI are presented using a Control Area Network (CAN) based communication protocol between master and slave inverters. The proposed control of the MSC-GCCI ensures an optimum and reliable operation of each of the parallel-connected inverters. The simulation and experimental results are presented to validate the proposed schemes for the MSC-GCCI.

articleTitle: Design of Zigbee based Wireless Stepper Motor Controller using FPGA
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: In this paper, design of wireless stepper motor controller using Verilog Hardware Description Language HDL is proposed and implemented on Altera Field Programmable Gate Array (FPGA). FPGA controller is used to control the stepper motor, Pulse-Width Modulation (PWM) method is used to rotate the motor through the desired angle speed and direction. Besides, features incorporated in the design are rotate the motor in directional to pause the rotation, to execute the rotation with varying speed in desired direction, return to zero and zero position detection. Stepper motor driver and magnetic sensor are used in this design. The stepper motor driver is to control the angle and direction of the stepper motor while the magnetic sensor is for the positioning application. Universal Asynchronous Receiver/Transmitter (UART) is used in this work to exchange the data with the ZigBee module, conversion of bytes need to be design in FPGA using Verilog HDL. The prototype is built and verified for its various functions.

articleTitle: An Efficient Topology for Inductive Wireless Power Transfer in Vehicular Application
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: In this paper, a current fed DC-DC converter topology is proposed for electrical vehicle battery charging of a wireless power transfer system. The proposed configuration is composed of a conventional current source inverter (CSI) interfaced to a diode bridge rectifier through a suitably modified tank circuit. It will be shown that an addition of a capacitor in the primary side transmitter loop results in the relieving of the CSI from supplying the reactive power demand while catering only to the active power demand of the load. Furthermore, this reduces the voltage stress of the CSI switches and thereby leads to reduced switching power losses, which further enhances the overall power conversion efficiency. The operating principle, mathematical analysis and design guidelines of the proposed converter are presented. An experimental verification using the laboratory developed prototype rated for 260 W is carried out and the resultes are presented. The obtained efficiency from the laboratory prototype is approximately 86.22% with a coupling coefficient of 17.88%.

articleTitle: Multi-Mode Power Management for Grid-Connected Photovoltaic System using Indirect Current Control Strategy
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: Integration of solar photovoltaic systems with the contemporary utility grid through the power electronic converters presents a new challenges and opportunities for providing ancillary services. Ancillary services include addressing energy need and rising power quality (PQ) issues. This scenario demands various control mechanisms to be embedded in the controller to provide above mentioned services. This paper presents an indirect decoupled current controller for multi-mode real and reactive power support to the grid. The proposed system works in three different modes as: 1) Excess power mode 2) Sufficient power mode and 3) Deficit power mode appropriate. The simulation model is developed for validating the proposed control logic under perturbing load condition and insolation change.

articleTitle: Reactive Power Compensation With Nine-Switch AC/AC Converter and Predictive Current Control Applied to a Variable Speed Driving Induction Motor
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)

authors.preferredName: Stefan Thiago Cury Alves dos Santos
José Roberto Boffino de Almeida Monteiro

abstract: The nine-switch AC/AC converter (NSC) is used as a substitute for the back-to-back converter (B2B). It is possible to use this converter for power factor (PF) correction during an AC motor driving due to its capability of current control on both three-phase terminals. This paper analyses the use of the Predictive Current Control (PCC) technique to operate a squirrel-cage induction motor (SCIM) connected to the grid through an NSC. Conditions of unity PF and reactive power compensation are evaluated for the grid-side while motor-side control is free to regulate the SCIM mechanical speed. Simulation results show that the NSC can operate with unity and leading power factor when using PCC in the existence of a mechanical torque in the SCIM's rotor shaft.

articleTitle: Implementation of Selective Harmonic Mitigation Scheme for Single Phase Inverter Systems
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: This paper presents a new scheme and procedure for implementation of selective harmonic mitigation (SHM) control scheme for single phase inverter systems. The detailed design of the control circuit has been discussed in detail.
