The unexplored facts and results of selective harmonic mitigation based single phase inverter system have been included in this paper.

articleTitle: Multifunctional Grid Interfaced Solar Based Microgrid with Seamless Mode Transition
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: This work presents an adaptive control approach of solar Photovoltaic (PV) based nonconventional energy system (NCES) with seamless changeover proficiency from an islanded mode (ILM) to grid-connected mode (GCM). The NCES has a capability to feed the load both in GCM and ILM and it operates smoothly during mode shifting from IL to GC and vice-versa. The unknown disruptions and uncertainties of NCES in GC mode are taken care by proportional plus multilayer modified third order sinusoidal signals integrator (P+M3rdOSSI) with multilayer harmonic decoupling network (MHDN). The concern like power fluctuations, DC offset, unbalance in voltage are successfully taken care by P+M3rdOSSI with MHDN. With the help of this algorithm, the sinusoidal quadrature fundamental component (SQFC) is extracted and reduces computational time. At the point of linkage (POL), the power quality gets improve with this control. It improves overall system performance as it operates adequately in steady state and transient conditions. To control the NCES in an ILM, the proportional plus resonant (P+R) based control algorithm is used. The steady state error gets reduced and system become robust with the help of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{P}+\mathrm{R}$</tex> based controller as compared to conventional PI control method, and hence zero steady-state error is achieve. A dual quadrature second order generalized integrator (DQSOGI) based PLL is used for precise and smooth synchronization and resynchronization of grid. DQSOGI based PLL improves system performance without affecting the stability. During frequency variation, it effectively follows the voltages of the grid and the load and it is adjustable to different conditions of grid. Moreover, total harmonic distortions (THDs) of the load and grid parameters are in the limits of the IEEE-519 standard.

articleTitle: Reconfigurable Two-Stage Solar PV -Battery Supported– Small Hydro System Based Micro-Grid
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: The operation of a double stage solar photovoltaic (PV)-battery supported small hydro system in reconfigurable modes like the grid connection (GC) and an islanded mode (IM) is reported. The small hydro system consists of a permanent magnet synchronous generator (PMSG) driven by an uncontrolled hydro turbine. Whenever the GC is not present this system works at IM and if the grid is available it synchronizes and operates in GC. A multilayer harmonics compensation phase locked loop (MHC-PLL) control is presented in this work. This PLL technique is used to estimate harmonics free positive sequence grid and hydro generator voltage phase angles for accurate and timely grid synchronization. A modified complex co-efficient (MCC) based filter is implemented to extract load currents fundamental component and controls the switching signals to voltage source converter (VSC) operating in both reconfigurable modes. An improved perturb and observe (IP&O) based maximum power point tracking (MPPT) control technique is used to extract maximum power from the solar photovoltaic (SPV) array. The boost converter based two-stage solar PV generation is controlled with its output to match with the DC-link voltage. The bidirectional converter (BDC) controls the bidirectional power flow in the battery by controlling its charging\discharging current.

Author Keywords: Multilayer Harmonic Compensation Phase Locked Loop (MHC-PLL)

articleTitle: Minimum DC Bus Capacitance Limit for STATCOM
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: Three-phase STATCOMs are popularly installed in distribution systems for maintaining voltage stability. With a view to enhancing the reliability and life-time of converters installed in such a system, constant effort is being made to minimize the use of failure-prone electrolytic capacitors. This necessitates the choice of optimal capacitance for the DC bus, leading to a tight design with reduced operating margin. However, the scope of reduction of the DC bus capacitance needs to be looked into without compromising the control, stability, and performance of the converter. Modeling of the converter yields operational limits associated with stability for a given DC bus capacitor design. This paper presents a model of a STATCOM, taking the impact of small DC bus capacitor into account. The minimum capacitance limit to ensure independent control of multiple control loops is analyzed and validated in this paper.

articleTitle: PV Characterization Method With Controlled Resolution
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: The characterization of Photo Voltaic (PV) panels plays a crucial role before installations and during operations of the panels, such as prediction of output, parameter estimation for modeling, efficiency evaluation, health monitoring, and verification of Maximum Power Point Tracking (MPPT) control. There are many methods of PV characterization; the performance of these methods is evaluated based on their speed, size, cost, reliability, power handling capacity. However, one index that is often not specified in many methods is the uniformity in sampling. With this, the resolution of sampling is varied, as the I-V curve of a PV panel is non-linear. This is not acceptable mainly during partial-shading when the I-V curve of the string has many transitions. In this work, a characterization method is developed with defined uniformity and defined minimum resolution throughout the I-V curve. A Buck-Boost converter with an input filter is used in this method, keeping in mind the cost, size, and power handling capacity. The converter is operated in closed-loop, where the input current and voltage are controlled, to achieve uniformity and resolution in sampling. For better dynamic performances, a double-loop control scheme is implemented, which mainly reduces the characterization time. Experimental results are included to validate the claims.

articleTitle: Behavioral Modeling of Perovskite Solar Cells and Study of its properties based on composition
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: The characteristics of organometallic halide per-ovskites material is being widely researched as a prospective absorber material for thin film solar cells with higher achievable conversion efficiency. In order to analyze power electronic systems using these advanced solar cell materials, it is necessary to obtain a behavioral model of the solar panel. In this paper, a heterojunction perovskite solar cell (PSC) is first modeled on SCAPS-ID (version 3.3.07) simulation software and tested for variation in the physical characteristics e.g., maximum power point, current density and voltage, efficiency, short circuit current density and open circuit voltage on varying the perovskite layer thickness. Device simulation studies for the material have shown maximum efficiency figures upto of 26.04% on SCAPS-ID platform. The forward and backward hysteresis characteristics obtained from SCAPS-ID simulation are modelled on MATLAB Simulink by mapping the characteristics into the conventional solar panel model. The behavioral model can be used for system level evaluation using power electronic converters.

articleTitle: Optimization based Variable Learning Factor Least Mean Square Algorithm to Control DVR in Infected Grid Systems
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: In this paper, a variable learning rate least mean square control algorithm has been proposed to control Dynamic Voltage Restorer for compensating the disturbances present in the supply source side of a distribution network. The proposed control algorithm is equipped with an optimization algorithm based on Slime Mould for the tuning of PI controller gains. The topology of the Dynamic Voltage Restorer presented in this paper is a voltage source converter with capacitor as an energy storage device that is utilized for the compensation of four various disturbances in the supply voltage viz. voltage sag, voltage swell, unbalance, and voltage distortions. System performance has been validated via simulation using MATLAB/Simulink.

articleTitle: Second Order Sliding Mode Observer Design for the Speed Estimation of DFIG
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: This paper proposes a new speed estimation technique based on the second order sliding mode observer (SOSMO) to observe/estimate the angular velocity/speed of the rotor of a double-fed induction generator (DFIG). The developed observer uses the measured stator currents and voltages from the stator terminal of the DFIG. Further, the estimated rotor position/angle is obtained by integrating the rotor speed. The paper also includes the convergence and stability proof for the designed observer. Finally, the designed observer is tested on a DFIG-based hardware test setup. The experimental results show that, during different dynamic and steady-state conditions, the proposed speed observer can determine the rotational speed and angle.

articleTitle: A New Soft-Switched DC-DC Buck Converter with Large Step Down Ratio
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: This paper proposes a new soft-switched dc-dc buck converter with large step-down ratio. The proposed converter uses a switched coupled-inductor to achieve high step-down ratio and a switched resonant-inductor cell for soft-switched transition of the semiconductor devices. The semiconductor switch turns on under ZV-ZCS condition and turns off with ZVS, while the diodes recover softly. The proposed converter is controlled with adaptive pulse frequency modulation (PFM) for soft-switched operation over a wide load range. Performance of the proposed converter has been verified with laboratory scale hardware prototype, rated with 42V-48V input and 5V, 25W output. The experimental results have endorsed the theoretical predictions.

articleTitle: A Comparative Study of Optimal Battery Storage and Fuel Cell for a Clean Power System in Remote Area
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: This paper investigates a comparative study on optimal sizing of fuel cell (FC) and battery energy storage (BES) systems coupled with solar photovoltaic (PV) and wind turbine (WT) for a remote area power system. Two system configurations: (1) PV-WT-BES and (2) PV-WT-FC are optimally sized based on actual annual data of wind, solar radiation, ambient temperature and load profile of a remote area community in South Australia. The costs of generation and storage units are considered based on real Australian market prices. The levelized cost of electricity (LCOE) is used as the objective function and appropriate optimization constraints are considered for each system. It is found that the BES technology is more economic than FC system for power system design in Australian remote areas. However, the PV-WT-FC system results in lower dumped energy. Sensitivity analysis is conducted to investigate the effects of the FC system price and its efficiency on LCOE and dumped energy of the system. The option of adding reactor/reformer to the FC system to produce hydrogen from the human waste is also studied in terms of optimal capacities, economic and dumped energy.

articleTitle: Power FET Degradation Test based on Thermal Equilibrium during Mission-Profile Characterization
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: Thermal stress is one of the prime causes leading to power semiconductor device failure. Therefore, a clear and accurate understanding of power switches' thermal degradation process is critical for proper design, reliability analysis, and lifetime prediction of power converters. This paper proposes a new degradation setup for the reliability assessment of power FETs based on thermal equilibrium during mission profile characterization. During a practical degradation process of the FETs, equilibrium junction temperature, and R<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">DS(ON)</sub> of the Device-Under-Test (DUT) are captured for post data processing to evaluate their Remaining-Useful-Lifetime (RUL). Mission profile tests with multiple load currents will be cycled until the device fails or the reliability parameters such as R<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">DS(ON)</sub> and the equilibrium junction temperature exceed a specific threshold value. This is repeated with different FETs at other ambient temperatures. It is hence possible to test four FETs at a time with reduced power drawn from the source. A complete electro-thermal simulation model and analysis of a SiC-MOSFET under inductive load switching operation on an H-bridge testing circuit has been successfully implemented in LTspice. The operation and benefits of the proposed characterization process have been proven by simulation and preliminary experimental results.

articleTitle: A Three-Phase Enhanced Boost Switched Inductor Z-Source Based Three-level Inverter-fed Induction Motor Drive
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: This paper presents an enhanced boost switched inductor (EBSI) Neutral-Point-Clamped Z-Source Inverter for three-level power conversion. The proposed inverter has high boost factor even with low shoot-through duty ratio and has low THD due to high modulation index in the entire ZSI operation. Maximum constant boost control scheme with carrier based SVPWM is used for the control of Z-source network. V/f ratio is maintained constant with the help of ZSI shoot-through based boosting of DC rail voltage above 29Hz of operation. Below 29Hz, SVPWM without ZSI shoot-through is used. A look up table is used to obtain the value of shoot-through duty ratio and modulation index needed to generate the correct phase voltage. The peak DC link voltage also changes in the same V/ f ratio which keeps the switching losses low unlike the conventional cases where the DC rail voltage is constant. MATLAB simulation of the proposed topology on a 5.4 HP, 400V three-phase V/f controlled induction motor drive, is used to verify the performance of the inverter circuit.

articleTitle: Enhanced Double Exponential Reaching Law based Sliding Mode Controller for Induction Motor Drives
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: A new reaching law for Sliding Mode Controller (SMC) called “Enhanced Double Exponential Reaching Law” (EDERL) is proposed in the paper. The reaching law is an improved version of Enhanced Exponential Reaching Law (EERL) and is tested on a three phase, 1hp, vector controlled Induction Motor(IM) drive. The proposed reaching law guarantees fast response, negligible chattering and superior dynamic tracking performance in the presence of uncertain disturbances compared to conventional reaching laws. The proposed reaching law is validated by simulation using Matlab platform and the hardware implementation is accomplished using dSPACE rti 1104 control desk.

articleTitle: A Single-Terminal Hybrid Scheme for Six-Phase Transmission Line Protection
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: This paper proposes a new single-ended fault classification scheme for six-phase transmission line (SPTL). The principle of current decomposition at the fifth-level is applied along with the discrete Fourier transform (DFT) and discrete symlet wavelet transform (DSWT) for classification of close-in relay faults, remote-end relay faults, evolving faults, and multi-location faults under modification of different fault parameters. The viability of the proposed hybrid technique is tested on a SPTL of 138 kV, 60 Hz using MATLAB. A widespread simulation study is accomplished and the proposed scheme has the capability to classify the faulty phase in less than 10 ms time. Simulation outcomes substantiate the usefulness of the proposed hybrid technique.

articleTitle: A Harmonic-Model based Resemblance between PI-SQIM, DI-OWIM, and DI-WRIM drives
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: High power Induction Machine (IM) drives are generally equipped with dual Voltage Source Inverters (VSIs), based on the ability of power conversion. Some of the widely known topologies are PI-SQIM, DI-OWIM, and DI-WRIM drives. In these IM drives, either two VSIs are employed on the stator (PI-SQIM and DI-OWIM) or one VSI each on the stator and rotor sides (DI-WRIM) which introduces harmonics into the IM drive. In this paper, the resemblances between the PI-SQIM, DI-OWIM, and DI-WRIM drives, in terms of the harmonic model of each drive, are discussed. The harmonic models of each drive are analyzed with the notion of direct and quadrature axis flux ripples that are introduced by each VSI. Analytical and simulation results are also presented to support the discussions on the resemblances between each drive system.

Author Keywords: Parallel-Inverter fed Squirrel Cage Induction Machine (PI-SQIM)
Double-Inverter fed Open-end Winding Induction Machine (DI-OWIM)
Double-Inverter fed Wound Rotor Induction Machine (DI-WRIM)

articleTitle: New Passive Auxiliary Circuit for Boost Converter to Provide Zero Input Current Ripple and Soft-Switching
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: In this paper, a new passive auxiliary circuit based boost converter is presented to provide soft-switching and zero input current ripple conditions. In this structure, the reverse recovery loss of the diode is minimized by turning off the diode under zero current switching (ZCS) condition. Besides, due to the effective performance of the auxiliary circuit, the switch turns off and on under zero voltage switching (ZVS) condition. Furthermore, the input current ripple has been minimized and this ripple is reduced nearly to zero. The performance of the proposed auxiliary circuit based boost converter has been investigated. The voltage gain, design procedure, efficiency analysis, and comparison results for the power converter are presented in the paper. Finally, simulation results are presented to validate the converter performance and its mathematical calculations.

articleTitle: A Novel AC Module with High gain Z-Source Converter and Pseudo DC-link inverter
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: The effects of partial shading in low power PV systems can be considerably reduced by using a single PV module of appropriate rating. Such a system is termed as the AC module in the literature and consists of a PV module along with the required power electronic circuitry, known as module integrated converter (MIC). The AC module integrated with the grid is required to operate at high efficiency and provide an output voltage of the expected magnitude and frequency. In this paper an efficient MIC with pseudo DC-link (pDC-l) for grid integration of AC module is proposed. The proposed MIC is claimed to be high efficient due to the fundamental frequency operation of the inverter. To obtain a pDC-l of required magnitude from single photovoltaic (PV) module, a high gain Z-source buck-boost converter (ZBBC) is used. It is followed by an unfolding circuit which operates at fundamental frequency to convert the pDC-l to sinusoidal output. The fundamental frequency operation reduces the switching losses without affecting the total harmonic distortion (THD). The operation of the ZBBC, when used to obtain a pDC-l output is analysed and a simple closed loop control is developed. The control ensures a pseudo DC-link voltage at the input of the H-bridge that acts as an unfolding circuit. The control also ensures power balance by controlling the current injected to the grid. Simulations of the proposed AC module with ZBBC cascaded with pDC-l inverter have been carried out using MATLAB/Simulink platform and the results are presented to validate the proposed MIC and its closed loop control.

articleTitle: Discontinuous Conduction Mode analysis of Single-phase Switched Boost Inverter with a dc load
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: As a potential alternative to conventional voltage source inverter (VSI), the single-phase Switched Boost Inverter (SBI) has been extensively researched owing to its ability to provide higher ac output voltage and superior reliability against shoot-through. Additionally, SBI can simultaneously operate with an ac load as well as a dc load, which can be connected in parallel to the dc bus capacitor. However, in literature, low-frequency ripple analysis and design of switch-impedance network have been presented with the assumption of continuous conduction mode (CCM) operation as well as the absence of a dc load. This paper aims to explore a more detailed analysis taking into account the possibility of SBI operation going into discontinuous conduction mode (DCM) with a dc load, which may result in voltage dip in the dc-link voltage. In accordance with the analysis, a modified design of passive elements is presented. The non-idealities in the circuit are also considered, which reveals that the selection of dc load has an impact on the boost factor as well. Finally, with the help of a hardware prototype, the single-phase SBI is operated in both CCM and DCM with the variation of the dc load to demonstrate the validity of the analysis.

articleTitle: A Wide Range Soft Switched Interleaved Boost Integrated L-L Type Full-Bridge DC-DC Converter
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: A new wide range soft switched interleaved boost integrated full-bridge DC-DC converter for PV and fuel cell applications is proposed in this paper. Fixed frequency PWM control is employed for output regulation. The proposed configuration has advantages such as soft switching across devices, wide ZVS range and very low input current ripple. The proposed configuration is simulated and corresponding results are discussed for a load of 200 W for 100% and 10% full-load conditions with input voltages of 22 V and 41 V.

articleTitle: Rapid Performance Prediction of Permanent Magnet Vernier Machine
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: This paper aims to propose a methodology for rapidly evaluating Permanent Magnet Vernier Machine (VPMM) performance. This procedure, includes electromagnetic determination of machine flux density, back-EMF, current, and torque using Finite Element Algorithm (FEA). For demonstration, two VPMMs with different slot types have also been analyzed. It has been demonstrated that openslot VPMM has superior performance compared to unity flux modulation ratio split-pole VPMM. However, it is possible for split-pole VPMM to surpass open-slot VPMM either by optimizing the shape of Flux Modulating Poles (FMP) or by employing the concept of advanced VPMM, i.e., with non-unity flux modulation ratio.

articleTitle: Performance of Droop Controller Combinations in Islanded Microgrids with Unbalanced Loads
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: Inverter based distributed generators (DGs) in microgrids can be controlled in either of the centralized, distributed or de-centralized approaches. Droop control involves the control of these inverters so as to mimic the behaviour of synchronous generators as in the bulk power system. The strategy is advantageous, as it is completely based on measurements made locally and does not need communication. The increasing penetration of single phase renewable energy sources in the modern distribution system increases the issue of asymmetry/unbalance in network. This work compares the performances of droop control combinations of distributed generators under unbalanced loading conditions. The performances under DG plug and play transitions and real and reactive power sharing among the DGs under unbalanced loads are studied through simulations on a modified 13 bus network and through experiments.

articleTitle: Open Switch Fault- DCM Mode Analysis of Neutral Point Clamped Inverter
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: Neutral Point Clamped (NPC) Multilevel Inverters (MLIs) find tremendous application in high and medium power and is proposed to be used in Electric Vehicles (EV). Compact size than other MLIs and advantages like low voltage stress on switches, high power quality, high DC bus voltage, reduced DC link current and low size phase conductors than 2-level inverters emphasis the use of NPC for EV applications. Due to the presence of large number of switches, switch faults are unavoidable during the operating lifetime of MLIs. The operation of NPC during open switch faults of inner switches are different and severe than outer switches open circuit faults. The shift of NPC from CCM to DCM mode of operation with inner switch fault causes the presence of abnormality in the pole voltage. In this paper, a voltage equation for analyzing the pole voltage during single inner switch open circuit fault of NPC inverter is proposed. The equation attests the occurrence of abnormal pole voltage during fault. The equation is verified by simulation and experimental results.

articleTitle: Design and Performance Optimization of Dual Rotor De-coupled Stator Multi-Phase Hybrid Magnetic Pole Permanent Magnet Synchronous Generator for Wind Turbine Application
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: The prime motive of the paper is to examine the design and performance optimization for a Dual Rotor Decoupled Stator Multi-Phase Hybrid Permanent Magnet Synchronous Generator (DRDCSMPH-PMSG) for wind turbine application. Such application requires the generator to be robust in nature, having higher fault tolerance capacity and high density of torque. Due to the dual rotor, the torque and the power density of proposed hybrid generator is high. The two sets of multi-phase (6-phase) winding arrangement, ensures high degree of fault tolerance capability of generator. For analysis of performance optimization of generator, the Finite Element Method (FEM) is selected, because of its greater accuracy. In order to design the generator optimally, magnetostatic and transient analyses are considered. For evaluating the performance of DRDCSMPH-PMSG, transient mode of analysis is selected. The generated EMF (electromotive force), electromagnetic torque vs time, percentage (%) THD, % torque ripple and many other characteristics are analyzed for proposed hybrid generator.

articleTitle: Optimal Proportional Resonant Control of Single PV fed Multilevel Converter Tied to Weak Grid
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: A new optimal solar photovoltaic (PV) system is introduced, where a proportional resonant controller is used for performance improvisation of a single PV fed grid-tied multilevel converter (SPGMC). The SPGMC configuration is developed using two H bridge cells and line frequency transformers. The grid current control is achieved using a proportional resonant (PR) current controller, which ensures improved steady-state and dynamic performance. Moreover, an error between the reference and the sensed grid current is minimized using the particle swarm optimization technique (PSO). The integral square error (ISE) is taken as an objective function and the mean of best values is selected for the PR controller. The merits of PSO based tuning over conventional tuning and PR controller for AC signals over conventional PI controllers lead to improved system performance. This optimal control is implemented for the closed-loop operation of a grid-tied solar photovoltaic (PV) system. This configuration has a single-stage MPPT controller, which reduces control complexity, and a single PV array, which minimizes the requirement of sensors. The performance of the PSO-PR based grid-tied system is tested under constant and variable solar irradiations. The PV array power is transferred to the grid at the unity power factor and the grid current harmonics are maintained under the IEEE 519 standard. Moreover, the system is tested under voltage sag and swell operation to handle weak grid situations. The system is modeled in MATLAB/Simulink and simulation results show the effectiveness of the grid-tied solar photovoltaic system.

articleTitle: MVZA-LMS with ESOGI-FLL Control for Solar PV-Battery System at Abnormal Grid Conditions
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: This paper represents a double stage solar photovoltaic (PV)-battery grid-interfaced system with improved power quality capabilities using MVZA-LMS (Modified Versoria Zero-Attraction Least Mean Square) based control. This control generates switching pulses for the voltage source converter (VSC). The power quality issues like minimisation the harmonics and compensating the load reactive power etc. are addressed by the grid interfaced VSC. The ESOGI (Enhanced Second Order Generalised Integrator) based frequency locked loop control is proposed to extract the sinusoidal grid voltages from polluted grid voltages. The DC link voltage and the battery current at load variations are regulated by using a BDC (Bidirectional Converter) control. The boost converter tracks the maximum power from a solar PV array and delivers this power to VSC via. DC link. The grid receives the active power from PV array in variable power mode. The battery storage is fulfilling load power requirement when the generated PV power is less. These controls are simulated into the MATLAB environment. Simulated results have exhibited good behavior at different dynamic conditions.

articleTitle: Availability Based Load Harmonic Compensation Using PV Inverter
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: With the proliferation of non-linear loads, the power quality particularly in the distribution level of the grid is deteriorating. The recent grid codes impose limit on the total demand distortion (TDD) and harmonic distortion (HD) level caused by these non-linear loads. The recent published researches focus on how to exploit the embedded photovoltaic (PV) inverters to meet the limit without further investing in custom power devices. In this regard, it is important to ensure that the reference current of the inverter should not exceed its maximum current rating to prevent the saturation of the current controller. The relevant control techniques either suffer from the saturation of the current controller or they fail to meet the TDD and HD levels individually. Therefore, to address these issues, an adaptive load harmonic compensation technique with the PV inverter is proposed in this work. The proposed technique adaptively determines the level of load harmonic compensation, thereby ensures the current controller does not saturate. Furthermore, this technique involves separate TDD control and HD control loop, to meet both the TDD limit and HD limit. The design procedure of the control loops is discussed. Finally, the proposed scheme is validated in MATLAB-Simulink platform.

articleTitle: Dynamic Performance of Coupled SIDO Buck Converter Operating in Current Mode and Voltage Mode Control
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: This paper studies the dynamic performances like audio-susceptibility, load regulation of coupled inductor single-input dual-output (CI-SIDO) buck converter operating in average current control (ACC) and voltage-mode control (VMC). First, the state-space model of the CI-SIDO buck is derived. Using the state-space model, the open-loop load regulation and audio-susceptibility is derived and analysed. Then, the closed-loop load regulation and audio-susceptibility are derived by closing the feedback loop for voltage-mode control (VMC) and average current control (ACC). Finally, the derived closed-loop transfer functions are verified through simulation results.

articleTitle: Mitigation of SSR in Series-Compensated DFIG-Based Wind Farms with STATCOMs using a Nonlinear Backstepping Control Scheme
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: A nonlinear backstepping control scheme is proposed in this work for the voltage source converter (VSC) used with the static synchronous compensator (STATCOM) in a doubly fed induction generator (DFIG)-based series compensated wind farm in order to mitigate sub-synchronous resonance (SSR) and improve the transient stability. The proposed scheme will regulate the reactive power requirement either by absorbing or supplying through the STATCOM for alleviating the SSR. At the same time, the tracking of other properties representing the dynamics of the STATCOM will be ensured through the proposed controller. The control inputs for the proposed nonlinear STATCOM controller are derived in a way that these satisfy the Lyapunov stability theory and ensure the appropriate tracking of all dynamics associated with the STATCOM. Simulation studies are conducted to justify the theoretical aspects of the proposed control scheme by developing the series compensated and grid-connected DFIG-based wind farm with the STACOM using MATLAB/SIMULINK platform. The high compensation level is considered for evaluating the performance under the worst case operating condition and the performance is compared with a traditional but finely tuned proportional integral (PI) controller in terms of eliminating fluctuations due to the SSR in the output responses of the DFIG-based wind farm.

articleTitle: Machine Learning based Fault Classification Approach for Power electronic converters
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: This research proposes a fault classification approach for power electronics converters (PECs) operating with the distributed generation systems. The proposed approach classifies and localizes the faults in PECs by adapting wavelet transforms and artificial neural networks. Initially, various failure mechanisms for power modules in PECs are identified to generate the fault data. Further, the detailed and approximate coefficients of the fault data at each frequency band are extracted using wavelet transform and used as inputs to the classifier. The ANN classifier estimates the non-linear relationship between the features and targets patterns to develop the fault classification mechanism. The numerical simulations are carried out for injecting various faults and degradation scenarios in both the legs of the inverter and developing the fault classifier in Plecs/MATLAB integration. The results showed 97.4% training accuracy with component failure classifier and 94.2% training accuracy with the classifier trained for 50% degradation in power module.

articleTitle: Efficiency Analysis of a 7.4 kW Dynamic Wireless Charging System for Electric Vehicle Through GaN Devices
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: The efficiency analysis is very important aspect which needs to investigate and enhance specially whenever it concerns to the electric vehicles (EVs) where range is a big challenge. Nowadays, the wireless charging scheme for EVs is the most popular technics in which dynamic charging technology provides better solutions to eliminate basic challenges of the static wireless charging system. The dynamic charging system mainly consists of different power converters and coil structure, in which efficiency of the power converters can be enhanced by using new generation wideband semiconductor devices while proper structural arrangement and materials of the coils help in boosting the efficiency of the coil section. In this work, a 7.4 kW dynamic wireless charging system is considered and the loss modeling of each power converters as well as coil section are demonstrated. The loss matrix is plotted with the help of MATLAB coding for two types of semiconductor devices i.e. silicon (Si) and gallium nitride (GaN), along with the output current and frequency. The comparative analysis is presented for both types of devices i.e. Si and GaN for a considered DWC system. Further, efficiency analysis is portrayed to show the impact of GaN devices. It is observed that approx 7 % (average) efficiency is enhanced below 4000 W power and beyond this, approx 3 % (average) efficiency is enhanced in the case of GaN compared to conventional device.

articleTitle: Two-Stage Deep Learning-based Wind Turbine Condition Monitoring Using SCADA Data
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: This paper proposes a two-stage data-driven methodology in condition monitoring (CM) of wind turbines (WTs). In the first stage, a fast and powerful network, namely a parallel generative adversarial network (PGAN) is proposed to resolve the problem of limited available information by generating artificial data. In the second stage, a robust deep network is designed based on a one-module Gabor filter oriented convolutional neural network and reformulation of a new loss function, namely robust deep Gabor network (RDGN). The experimental dataset of 3MW wind turbines in Ireland is used to verify the effectiveness of the proposed method and demonstrate the superiority of the proposed two-stage method in comparison with several state-of-the-art methods in terms of accuracy and reliability.

articleTitle: Two-stage Robust Management of PEV Parking Lots Coupled with Multi-energy Prosumers under Load and Energy Market Uncertainty
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: Development of multi-energy integration for the commercial/Industrial sector introduces a high level of interdependency between different energy carriers which requires integrated modeling of these multi-energy systems (MESs). Transportation electrification such as the integration of plug-in electric vehicles (PEVs) has the potential to have a significant effect on the operation of commercial MESs which are equipped with large scale PEVs' parking lots. Although the development of energy management models to optimally integrate PEVs into MES leads to higher benefits, the associated operational uncertainties can bring additional costs for system operators. Ignoring these uncertainties can result in nonoptimal or even infeasible operational solutions for MES facilities. In this paper, a two-stage robust energy management model has been proposed for MESs equipped with PEV parking facilities to optimally schedule MES facilities and its interaction with upstream network, while, supplying the required PEV charging patterns, considering the uncertainties of MES loads and energy market prices. The proposed model is developed as a min-max-min optimization problem which is solved through a column-and-constraint methodology, recasting the tri-level problem into a first-stage min problem and a second-stage maxmin problem. The second-stage problem is solved through duality theory and Big-M linearization technique. A comprehensive case study has been conducted to evaluate the effectiveness of the proposed model. According to the obtained results, MESs are able to supply PEVs and multi-energy loads, while participating in upstream network energy market with operational solutions that are robust against uncertainties, resulting in extra benefits and lower operational costs.

articleTitle: Dual Active Bridge based Micro-Inverter for Standalone Renewable Energy Systems with Low DC Link Capacitance
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: Micro-inverters are required to interface PV generation directly with AC loads or grid at low power levels. A typical microinverter consists of a DC/DC conversion stage, followed by an inverter stage. Dual active bridge (DAB) converter appears to be a promising candidate for use in the DC/DC converter stage in a microinverter since it offers several features like high voltage gain, galvanic isolation, zero voltage switching, etc., which are highly desirable for microinverters applications. A micro-inverter topology is presented in this paper which is based on the dual active bridge converter. The proposed topology also incorporates active power decoupling (APD) by supplying the low frequency component of single phase AC power drawn by the load without using any extra switch. APD allows reduction in the required value of DC link capacitance without having a large voltage ripple. This obviates the use of electrolytic capacitors, which generally have a short operating life and are considered a weak link in power electronic systems. The paper describes the modelling of DAB for closed loop control, and the control system for 100 Hz power decoupling. The proposed microinverter topology has been simulated in PLECS, and the simulation results are presented here.

articleTitle: Active Power Decoupling for Differential Buck Inverter using Virtual Resistor
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: Single phase inverter DC link contains low frequency current ripple at twice the grid frequency. To supply this ripple current, bulky electrolytic capacitors are used which reduces the reliability of the system. This paper proposes a simple control scheme for active power decoupling of grid connected differential buck inverter by implementing virtual resistors in parallel to filter capacitances. Basic operating principle and circuit design are explained in detail. Resistance emulation is achieved using a proper control strategy to damp out the LC oscillation. The scheme reduces sensor count by one. System is simulated for 2 kW load and effectiveness of the scheme is demonstrated.

articleTitle: An Electric Vehicle Charger Based on Vienna Rectifier and Resonant LLC Converter
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: In this work, a medium and high power rating electric vehicle (EV) charger based on Vienna rectifier (VR) and half bridge resonant inductor-inductor-capacitor (LLC) converter, is presented. The two switch VR forms the front-end converter, and performs active power factor correction (PFC), by operating under continuous conduction mode (CCM). Moreover, its output voltage is regulated by an outer voltage control loop, in a two loop pulse width modulated (PWM) control. The EV battery is charged using constant voltage (CV) and constant current (CC) controller by a pulse frequency modulation (PFM) based half bridge LLC converter. The DC-DC conversion stage of this charger is soft switched due to zero voltage switching in LLC converter. Simulation results and its performance under steady state and dynamic conditions, are presented. Moreover, the power quality (PQ) and steady state results are verified and presented for a 5.6kW experimental prototype.

articleTitle: Control of Switched-Capacitor Based Fifth-order Buck-Boost Converter
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: A fifth-order switched-capacitor based buck-boost converter is proposed in this article. Presence of switched-capacitor provides a wider duty ratio range for bucking operation in addition to boosting feature at higher duty ratios. Principle of operation is explained first, followed by steady-state performance analysis using the time-domain analysis. Using the capacitor and inductor voltage equations, the expressions for ripple currents/voltage are formulated. A brief comparison of other existing buck-boost topologies is presented to bring out the salient performance features of the proposed converter topology. Voltage buck-boost features are demonstrated first in simulation and then later in the experiment. A 30 ~ 50 Watt 50 kHz prototype topology is constructed for experimental studies. Sample experimental measurements are presented for concept validation. They are found to be in line with theoretical derivations.

articleTitle: Efficient Energy Recovery and Boosting the Voltage Gain of a Soft-Switched Flyback Converter
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: This paper presents a new soft-switched flyback converter with an active clamp circuit, used to recover the leakage energy of the flyback transformer. The trapped leakage energy is further utilized for charging a clamping capacitor, connected in series with the input supply. Thus, overall voltage gain of the flyback converter is boosted up. All the semiconductor switches of this flyback converter are operated under soft-switching conditions and the semiconductor diodes are commutated softly. Performance of the proposed converter has been successfully verified through hardware experimentation of a laboratory prototype.

articleTitle: An Interaction Less Duo Control Strategy for Bi-polar Voltage Source Converter in Renewables Integrated Multi-Terminal HVDC (MTDC) Grids
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: The PVF or PV<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>F double droop control is commended for its ability to regulate both the dc voltage and frequency in a decentralized approach. However, a convincing response is not achieved due to an interaction between the droop characteristics of dc voltage and frequency. This interaction affects the dc voltage and frequency support of the AC system surrounded the Multi-Terminal HVDC (AC-MTDC) grid. To overcome this effect a interaction less Duo control strategy is proposed in this paper, which takes the advantage of a Bi-polar Voltage Source Converter (B-VSC) topology in the MTDC grid. The virtue of the proposed control technique is emphasized by comparing it with the existing PV<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>F double droop control along with two case studies. The validation of interaction less Duo control strategy is carried out on five terminal CIGRE DC grid benchmark model integrated into two area power system, which is simulated in PSCAD/EMTDC software.

articleTitle: Alternate power flow controller for voltage control in an unbalanced distribution network
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: This paper proposes the use of power flow controller based on multi-winding transformer (MWT) for voltage control in a three phase unbalanced distribution network. The power flow controller can be taken as an add-on block to the existing distribution transformer and its parameters can be adjusted to control voltage magnitude and angle at various buses in the distribution network. The mathematical model of the controller is derived for implementation of load flow program on three phase unbalanced distribution network. The optimal values for controller parameters, for improving voltage profile and reducing unbalance in the distribution network, are found using Grey Wolf Optimization (GWO) with simulation studies carried out on 26 bus test network.

articleTitle: An On-Board Fast Charger using New Bridgeless PFC Converter with Reduced DC-Link Capacitance
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: This paper deals with a new approach to design a fast charger for electric vehicle, which consists of a new bridgeless (BL) Zeta PFC (Power Factor Correction) converter with reduced size of DC-link capacitance cascaded by a buck converter. The battery fast charging is provided based on a new approach of operating the PFC converter at increased DC-link voltage, as compared to the conventional slow chargers. This implies to the reduced size of DC-link capacitance, as the value of DC-link capacitance varies inversely with respect to the DC-link voltage. The proposed BL Zeta converter has lower device voltage stress, which ensures a high-power density and better efficiency during fast charging at the battery end. A buck converter is used to control the battery current during constant current and constant voltage modes. Moreover, the operation of two converters in the discontinuous conduction mode (DCM) gives the benefit of fewer sensors as sensing of input side quantities is avoided. It is shown that with the proposed topology, the battery charging can be achieved 8 times faster than conventional BL Zeta converter.

articleTitle: A Reduced Switch Count Boost Inverter (RSC- BI) Topology with Triple Voltage Gain
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: For multilevel inverter topologies, the boosting feature is an important aspect for the application related to the low voltage input obtained from solar PV for high voltage application. The proposed RSC-BI aims for the higher voltage gain with lower device count. The proposed RSC-BI uses eight switches with two capacitors for seven-level (7L) waveform having triple voltage gain. In this paper, a detailed comparison has been included along with the simulation and experimental results. All these results and discussion shows the better performance of the proposed RSC-BI.

articleTitle: High-Gain Non-Isolated Battery Integrated DC-DC Boost Converter for Electric Vehicle
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: In this paper, a two-switch high-gain non-isolated battery integrated boost converter (HGNIBIBC) is proposed and analyzed. This converter integrates the renewable source with the energy storage device such as a battery for increasing the driving range and reducing the peak power required from the source. The battery current is in the form of pulses which decrease the charging time for the battery and increases the capacity retention rate. To design the converter control, a small-signal model for each power operating state is defined. The control strategy to deal with varying load torque and source power are essentially addressed in this paper. Steady-state and dynamic results are presented to demonstrate the application of proposed converter in the electric vehicle operation.

articleTitle: A Novel Coupled Inductor Based Active Balancing Technique for Ultracapacitors
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: A novel active buck-boost equalizer with a coupled inductor is proposed here for balancing ultracapacitors (UC) strings connected in the form of a matrix configuration. As a coupled inductor is used instead of an inductor, the number of switches and inductor windings required for balancing is reduced to N/2 and (N-P), respectively, where N is the number of UC cells to be balanced, and P is the number of parallel strings. The proposed balancing circuit requires only a single pair of complementary pulse width modulation (PWM) signals to balance the entire UCs in the UC strings. Hence, control complexities are significantly less as compared to the existing active voltage balancing methods. The effectiveness of the proposed topology is verified in the MATLAB/simulation platform and validated experimentally.

articleTitle: Power Quality Improvement strategy for DSTATCOM using Adaptive Sign Regressor LMF Control
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: A novel power quality improvement strategy based on Sign Regressor Least Mean Fourth (SRLMF) control technique is proposed for DSTATCOM. In this control technique, SRLMF algorithm derives the fundamental component of load currents and these current components are used to obtain the reference signals for optimal switching of the Voltage source converter. Here, SRLMF control scheme is utilized to improve the power quality of the distribution system, owing to its superior performance in harmonics mitigation, load balancing and power factor correction. The effectiveness of this control scheme is compared with a conventional Least Mean Fourth control on the basis of convergence and harmonics elimination. The simulation results demonstrate that SRLMF limits THD of grid currents are within the IEEE standards, which effectively improves the power quality in the connected system.

Author Keywords: Sign Regressor Least Mean Fourth control

articleTitle: Review of Front-end DC-DC Boost Converters in Two-stage Micro-inverters
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: The low output voltage of solar photovoltaic (PV) panel makes it incompatible for directly powering the dc-link of the voltage source inverter (VSI). As a result of which two-stage micro-inverter (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mu$</tex>-I) configurations came into existence. The first stage enhances the PV voltage to a standard recognized dc level, and the second stage finally produces the bipolar output voltage. This paper presents a review of front-end dc-dc boost converters in a typical two-stage <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mu$</tex>-Is. Various boosting techniques incorporated in the converters to attain high gain are illustrated and compared based on their voltage gain expressions. Impact of non-idealities, components count, common input-output terminal and input current continuity are some of the points considered to make the final verdict about the presented voltage boosting techniques.

articleTitle: Self-Reliant Feature in DC-DC Converters for Open Circuit Faults
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: With vast applications of dc-dc converters in grids and micro grids, the need of a vigorous converter with fault tolerant capability becomes very important. Dual active bridge (DAB) and series resonant converters (SRC) are extensively used in smart transformers. Hence the fault tolerant feature is a must in such converters in order to maintain a continuous operation with voltage and power regulation. This paper proposes the analysis of single or two switch open circuit fault on primary and secondary side of DAB and SRC. The self-reliant nature of converter in achieving fault tolerance with the help of phase shift between its input and output side is also discussed. The proposed analysis is tested on 1kW, 250V DAB and SRC prototype. The proposed correction for open circuit fault on SRC is simulated in PLECS software.

articleTitle: Operation and Control of Integrated Dual-Output Converter interfacing non-linear loads
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: Integrated Dual-Output Converter (IDOC) topology can be used to interface two dc-outputs, the magnitude of one is higher and the other is lower than input dc voltage. In this work, IDOC topology has been designed and developed to interface non-linear loads powered from a single current limited dc power supply (DCPS). The third port of IDOC is interfaced to battery storage, and it has been demonstrated in this work that the presence of this storage enables reduction in rating of DCPS and also facilitates energy management. The modes of operation of the converter, system modeling, and closed loop controller design for IDOC has been presented. In addition, phase-shift change-over PWM (PS-CPWM) control scheme has been proposed to enable smooth transition between battery charging and discharging modes, and its performance has been compared to conventional control approaches. Using simulation, dynamics of IDOC, closed loop control system behavior, and energy management has been presented.

articleTitle: Model Predictive Control for Modular Electric Vehicle Charger
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: In this paper, a power converter architecture is implemented for charging of electric vehicles (EVs), which is based on a cascaded multi-level converter with an integrated split-energy storage units. The power interface between each submodule and EV is connected to an isolated bidirectional DC-DC converter. A unit-template based model predictive control (MPC) is implemented to improve power quality and reliability of the distribution network while charging an EV battery. The MPC approach in this paper, consists of three steps: The first step is an optimization problem i.e., current-control in MPC, the second step is the design making step regarding weighting factor and the third is the fault detection and action control. Further, state of charge balancing is also achieved using MPC to charge/ discharge all split battery storage units at same rate. Finally, the control is verified by simulating the system in MATLAB/Simulink at different operating modes.

articleTitle: A Novel Directly-solvable Non-iterative Load Flow Model for Radial Distribution System Studies
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: Load flow problems in electricity distribution systems (EDS) are generally solved through iterative methods such as Newton-Raphson, Gauss-Seidel, Forward-backward Sweep-based methods, etc. These methods are subject to problems such as poor convergence for EDSs with high R/X ratio branches and huge mathematical/programing burden in some cases. Moreover, in EDS studies such as power loss minimization, energy management, EDS planning/expansion, etc., load flow calculations need to be conducted alongside the required objective function and the related constraints of the study. To solve such models, optimization techniques such as metaheuristic methods, are used in which load flow calculation is conducted in each iteration, bringing extra mathematical burden. To address these limitations, this paper presents a new directly solvable and non-iterative load flow model which is developed using a new bus indexing procedure. A connectivity matrix is introduced to characterize the configuration of EDS and provide a feasible general representation of load flow equations. This enables the proposed modified load flow equations to be mergeable in any type of EDS study as model constraints. Moreover, unlike previous iterative models, it can be solved directly through standard optimization packages in a single shot with no need to further iterative optimization procedures, such as metaheuristic methods. This results in a moderate mathematical and programing burden. The 33-bus system is employed to evaluate the effectiveness of the proposed load flow model. The obtained results are reported and compared with forward-backward sweep-based load flow as a benchmark. Accordingly, it is shown that the proposed model maintains the same outcome without using iterative optimization techniques.

articleTitle: A Spectral Clustering Based Distributed Control of Distributed Energy Resources (DERs) Integrated Power Distribution System
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: Motivated by the government's clean energy targets, the penetration of Distributed Energy Resources (DER) is increasing. These DERs interconnections bring the added generation and storage capacity at the distribution level. Also, with the increasing implementation of smart inverters and Advanced Distribution Management Systems (ADMS), the flexibility of the DERs can be leveraged to solve the distribution grid issues like over abnormal voltages, intermittencies, and thermal overloads. The proposed work focuses on the development of a robust distributed control architecture to control and optimally manage the load and PV variations using energy storage by creating the virtual clusters of the distribution grid.

articleTitle: High Stability Adaptive LDO using Dynamic Load Sensing for Low Power Management of Wireless Sensor Networks
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: Presented in this paper is the design of a low-dropout voltage regulator implemented in 65nm CMOS technology for low power management of wireless sensor networks for IoT technology. High stability is achieved using a dynamic load sensing technique where the sensed load current adjusts the bias of the error amplifier. The dynamic mechanism provides low/high bias current to the error amplifier as the load current decreases/increases, respectively. The LDO adapts and transforms from a 2-stage configuration at light-loads to a 3-stage configuration at high-load conditions for a more current-efficient system. Two power transistors are activated depending on the load conditions, with the main power transistor activated only if the load current is greater than the threshold current I<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">on</sub>of 919.11μA, allowing for wide range of load application from 0 to 100 mA. Simulation results confirm that adaptive biasing technique through dynamic load sensing and subthreshold operation of the system enables the LDO to achieve ultra-low quiescent current of 930.21nA with power consumption of 744.17nW at no-load. A regulated output voltage of 600mV from 800mV to 1.2V supply voltage with a dropout voltage of 135mV.

articleTitle: Design and Analysis of Fourth Order ZVS Output Filter for Three-Level Buck Envelope Tracking Power Supply
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: With the increased data speeds, the bandwidth requirements of communication systems are getting higher and higher, so are the losses associated with the radio frequency (RF) transmitters in base stations. Envelope Tracking (ET) is a power supply modulation technique that improves the efficiency of the lossy linear power amplifier of the transmitter by adjusting the voltage magnitude according to the peak of the signal that is being amplified. This paper presents detailed guidelines to design `zero voltage switching (ZVS) filters' for the multi-phase buck converters in bandlimited ET applications. The results of the proposed filter while tracking a 4G LTE envelope signal are compared with that of the standard Legendre Papoulis filter. The proposed filter design achieves better tracking speed, ZVS turn-on, and maintains current balancing among phases in the multi-phase buck converter. The converter with the proposed filter attains a peak efficiency of 97.5% and efficiencies above 90% for most of the operating range.

articleTitle: Minimum Leakage Inductance for Soft-switching of Dual-Active Half-Bridge DC-DC Converter
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: In DC-DC converters like Dual Active Bridge (DAB) and Dual Active Half Bridge (DAHB) where leakage inductance also acts like power transfer inductance, it is important to have optimum leakage inductance, especially in high frequency applications. High value of leakage inductance result in high RMS current through transformer with higher conduction losses in transformer and switches, whereas, low value of leakage inductance result in loss of Zero Voltage Switching (ZVS) turn-on at lower power level with higher switching losses. This paper presents analytical derivation of minimum leakage inductance and dead-time for ZVS turn-on of switches in Current Source Voltage Source (CSVS) type of Dual Active Half Bridge (DAHB) DC/DC Converter which can be used to design optimal leakage inductance.

articleTitle: 13.56MHz High Power Half-Bridge GaN-HEMT Resonant Inverter Achieving 99% Power Efficiency
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: High-power inverters with high frequency have been required for progressing technologies such as wireless power transfer (WPT) and plasma processing. Recently, gallium nitride high electron mobility transistor (GaN-HEMT) is getting lots of attention from the viewpoint of fast switching ability and low power consumption. However, GaN-HEMT inverters are difficult to be operated in over several kW because of its low drain-source breakdown voltage. In other words, the conventional half-bridge GaN-HEMT inverter can output high power only for the small load resistance less than several- Ω. This paper overcomes this difficulty by implementing an impedance conversion network in the prior stage of the series resonator. The proposed topology realizes not only high-power from low drain-source voltage but also the sine wave output with very low harmonics. 3kW output to 50Ω load at 13.56MHz is theoretically designed, and verified by computer simulations. And also, the experimental prototype using GaN-HEMTs achieves the high efficiency of 99.43% at 13.56MHz and 471W.

articleTitle: MMCC based PMSG for Oceanic Wave Energy Conversion System
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: This paper presents the use of a Modular Multilevel Cascaded converter (MMCC) based Permanent magnet synchronous generator (PMSG) to harness the Oceanic Wave Energy (OWE). A direct-drive PMSG with Wells Turbine operates at a variable speed in a wide speed range and gives optimized power output using an MPPT algorithm. In this paper, MMCC is used to connect a PMSG operating at variable voltage and variable frequency to a fixed voltage fixed frequency grid in a single stage with the full control over grid-side current and machine side current. Analytical expressions supported by simulation results are presented to validate the performance of the proposed scheme.

articleTitle: A New Protection Scheme for DC Microgrid using Numerical Computational Method
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: AC protection schemes are well understood and mature. On the other hand in the DC system, the development of protection schemes is the main challenge for the researcher because of additional power electronic devices. Some protection schemes are developed on the principle of the rate of change of current but it may mall operate for the noisy system. In this article, a protection scheme is developed based on the numerical computational method(Trapezoidal method) to fast detection of the fault and also to avoid the effect of the noise. The proposed protection scheme is validated on the ring type DC microgrid for different fault conditions and tested through MATLAB/Simulink Simulator.

articleTitle: A New Single-Switch Three-Phase AC-AC Boost Converter
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: In this paper, a new three-phase ac-ac boost converter is proposed, which utilizes single switch for the power conversion. The utilization of a single switch reduces the switching power loss compared to its conventional counterpart. Moreover, the proposed converter demonstrates moderate total harmonic distortion in the input line current and facilitates high input power factor operation. Furthermore, the proposed topology exhibits superior performances under sudden change in the load power factor and duty cycle variation. All the simulations are carried out in MATLAB/Simulink environment and a corresponding scaled down laboratory test platform is established. The simulation and the experimental results validate the excellent performances of the proposed ac-ac boost converter topology.

articleTitle: Control of Solar-Battery Fed Synchronous Reluctance Motor Drive for Light Electric Vehicle with Range Extension
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: This paper presents a solar photovoitaic (PV)-battery integrated system for the light electric vehicle (LEV) based on a synchronous reluctance (SyR) motor drive with extended range. Since the system is a battery operated, therefore the power to the motor is supplied from the battery and it is also charged by the PV array and by the regenerative braking. To extract maximum power from a PV array, an incremental conductance (InC) method based maximum power point tracking (MPPT) is used. The battery charging by the PV array and by the regenerative braking, increases the overall range of the LEV, voltage source inverter (VSI) is utilized for supplying power to SyR motor, from the battery/PV array. The efficacy of this system is verified by simulation in MATLAB/Simulink.

articleTitle: Power Management of a Grid Interactive PV - Fuel Cell Hybrid System with Power Dispatch to the Grid Using Modified LMS Control
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: Hybrid systems comprising renewable energy sources based distributed energy generation connected to the grid with energy storage systems increase the cost and control complexity. But, to provide reliable power to the grid, storage systems are essential. Here, a grid-connected Photovoltaic-Fuel cell hybrid system with a fixed power dispatch to the grid using a modified least mean square control has been proposed. This has been realized to control the power flow from the sources and the load. Any variation in the photovoltaic power is balanced by power from the fuel cell by introducing a power management scheme. The change in power flow to the load arising at the transient stage due to the slow response of the fuel cell is met by power support from the grid. Moreover, the hybrid system mitigates power quality issues at the point of interconnection in the grid. The performances of the system during steady-state and transient conditions are verified by extensive simulation analysis with MATLAB with its simpower system block set.

articleTitle: Mathematical Modeling of Flat Plate Solar Collector
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: The solar energy collector is the heart of a flat-plate solar collector (FPSC) system. This is designed and developed for operation in the low-temperature range (ambient to 60°C) or in the medium temperature ranges (ambient to 100°C). FPSC is designed and developed to absorb incident solar energy, convert it into heat and transfer the heat energy to a gas or fluid which is in contact with it. FPSC absorbs both the diffused and beam radiation. This paper deals with the study of solar intensity on a FPSC for different tilt conditions and derivation of the mathematical modelling of solar radiation on an inclined plane surface.

articleTitle: Three-Phase Radial EMTP and Stealthy Attack Detector for Distribution Systems
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: This paper presents an algorithm for obtaining the transient solution for three-phase radial networks. The proposed Radial EMTP (electromagnetic transient program) is based on a backward-forward sweep technique which exploits the radial nature of distribution network. Using this Radial EMTP, a technique is developed to detect stealthy attacks targeted against distribution systems. This method requires lesser computational resources as compared to conventional EMTP programs. This paper also develops a transient model for three-phase synchronous generators which is compatible with the proposed three-phase radial EMTP. The proposed technique has been tested on 5-bus three-phase system which is powered by two synchronous generators. The proposed Radial EMTP has been benchmarked with Opal-RT's HYPERSIM and it is shown that the proposed technique can identify stealthy attacks.

articleTitle: DC-Offset Rejection Approaches for Single-Phase Frequency-Locked Loop
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: Frequency-fixed implementation of a single-phase frequency-locked loop (FLL) has been reported to enhance the FLL's dynamic performance when the supply voltage is sinusoidal or harmonically distorted. However, when dc-offset is present in the supply voltage, a dc-offset rejection (DC-OR) stage is usually incorporated in the FLL implementation. How the DC-OR stage affects the FLL's dynamic performance is one gap that exists in the literature. Consequently, this paper focuses on evaluating the effect of the DC-OR stage on the FLL's performance by coupling and decoupling the DC-OR stage and the FLL. Decoupling is achieved by fixing the frequency of the DC-OR stage at the supply voltage's nominal frequency. However, this introduces a phase-offset error at the FLL output when the supply voltage experiences a frequency deviation. To address this issue, a phase-offset compensation approach is developed. Through experimental studies, accuracy of the phase-offset compensation approach is verified. Furthermore, it is shown that farther the point of decoupling and the FLL output, faster is the FLL response. Therefore, a frequency-adaptive FLL can achieve faster response than its frequency-fixed counterpart when the effect of dc-offset rejection stage is considered.

articleTitle: Testing of SiC Voltage Source Inverter fed Induction Motor Drive and its Control with Output Sinusoidal LC filter
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: In this paper, some experimental results of an in-house designed and developed SiC MOSFETs based voltage source inverter (VSI) feeding an open-loop v/f controlled squirrel cage induction motor (SQIM) drive have been presented at different operating conditions, and the temperature of the heat sink has been measured to ascertain its safe long-run operation. A sinusoidal LC filter has also been designed and rotor-flux oriented control (RFOC) of SiC VSI fed SQIM drive with the filter has been implemented to control the SQIM. Active damping (AD) technique has been used to improve the stability of the drive at different operating points ensuring its satisfactory steady-state as well as dynamic performance.

articleTitle: A Coupled Inductor Based Ćuk Microinverter for Grid Connected Photovoltaic Applications
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: A single phase single stage current source microin-verter scheme is proposed in this paper which can extract maximum power from a low voltage photovoltaic (PV) panel and can supply it to a single phase utility grid of (220 - 230) V at unity power factor (UPF). High voltage gain at the output stage is achieved by employing a Coupled inductor based Cuk topology at the input stage of the inverter. Energy trapped in the leakage inductance of the coupled inductor is utilized at the grid side by employing a coupling capacitor. Voltage spikes that appear across the power switch during the turn off process, are controlled by using a passive snubber. Discontinuous mode of conduction (DCM) of the magnetizing current is adopted to ensure simplicity in design of the controller. Soft turn on of the power switch is experienced by utilizing the phenomenon of resonance that occurs between the snubber capacitor and the magnetizing inductance during high frequency turn on period, thereby improving the overall system efficiency. The operating principle, followed by the current control strategy for the proposed microinverter is discussed in details. The viability and efficacy of the proposed scheme is verified by extensive simulation studies.

articleTitle: Proposing New Analytical Competitiveness Indices to Assess Total Electricity Market Deviation Possibility
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: Evaluating the potential of market power and collusion between market player, as the deviant behaviors in competitive electricity market, can provide more clear insights when assessing power market dynamics. Although many research works have explored this issue, no study has yet proposed an analytical cumulative index to assess the possibility of deviant behavior in a power market as a whole. The main goal of this paper is to propose accurate and analytically indices to evaluate the effects of deviation possibilities for individual market players, and accordingly, the power market as a whole. These indices evaluate both bid-based and capacity-based types of two strategic behaviors, i.e., market power and the collusion between market players. Our proposed competitiveness indices are analytical and can be calculated for different load levels easily, so they are more convenient for large networks. Since, the proposed model is analytical, it can be directly solved in a single shot with off-the-shelf softwares with no need to further trial-based methodologies. The IEEE 24-bus Test System (RTS) has been considered for simulation purposes.
